FAERS reporting identified RVAEs across included IVT therapies, but cannot establish incidence, causality, or comparative risk, underscoring the need for vigilant reporting and ongoing post-marketing safety surveillance.

records.title: EVALUATING THE EFFICACY AND SAFETY OF TOPICAL DIFLUPREDNATE IN PATIENTS WITH CHRONIC CENTRAL SEROUS CHORIORETINOPATHY.

content.title: EVALUATING THE EFFICACY AND SAFETY OF TOPICAL DIFLUPREDNATE IN PATIENTS WITH CHRONIC CENTRAL SEROUS CHORIORETINOPATHY.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To evaluate the efficacy and safety of topical difluprednate ophthalmic emulsion 0.05% in chronic central serous chorioretinopathy (cCSCR) and compare its outcomes with oral eplerenone and observation.

Methods

This pilot open-label randomized controlled trial included patients with cCSCR of ≥3 months' duration or relapsing cases with subfoveal or juxtafoveal leakage on angiography. After baseline assessment, patients were randomized into three groups: topical difluprednate, oral eplerenone, or observation. All participants were followed monthly for 3 months. Changes in best-corrected visual acuity, optical coherence tomography parameters, retinal sensitivity, and adverse events were documented.

Results

A total of 53 adults (mean age 42.6 ± 9.5 years; 90.6% male) were enrolled. Complete resolution of subretinal fluid occurred in 90% (n = 18) of the patients in the difluprednate group, 45% (n = 9) in eplerenone group, and 23% (n = 3) patients in the control arm ( P < 0.001). The difluprednate group showed significantly greater reductions in subfoveal choroidal thickness and improvements in 3-mm microperimetry thresholds compared with the observation group ( P = 0.012 and P = 0.022, respectively). It also demonstrated the largest decrease in central macular thickness, although this was not statistically significant ( P = 0.19). Ocular hypertension developed in 30% of difluprednate-treated eyes and was controlled with topical antiglaucoma medication.

Conclusion

Topical difluprednate produced superior anatomical and functional improvements in subretinal fluid resolution, subfoveal choroidal thickness reduction, and retinal sensitivity within 3-mm when compared with oral eplerenone and observation. Thus, with a manageable safety profile, it may serve as an effective therapeutic option for cCSCR.

records.title: Incidence and Outcomes of Retinal Detachment After Pars Plana Vitrectomy for Symptomatic Floaters.

content.title: Incidence and Outcomes of Retinal Detachment After Pars Plana Vitrectomy for Symptomatic Floaters.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To report the incidence, clinical characteristics, and visual and anatomical outcomes of rhegmatogenous retinal detachment (RRD) following pars plana vitrectomy (PPV) for symptomatic vitreous floaters.

Methods

This retrospective, consecutive case series evaluated 256 eyes of 205 patients who underwent PPV for symptomatic floaters with a minimum 6-month follow-up. Main outcomes included RRD incidence, single surgery anatomical success, final reattachment rates, and visual acuity (VA) changes.

Results

Over a mean follow-up of 31.8 months, 14 of 256 eyes (5.5%) developed an RRD at a median of 19 days postoperatively. At presentation, 78.6% of detachments were macula-on. Final anatomical success was achieved in 100% of eyes with all successfully maintaining reattachment without the need for long-term silicone oil. Among eyes that developed RRD, median logMAR visual acuity changed from 0.00 (20/20) preoperatively to 0.18 (20/30) at the final visit, though this did not reach statistical significance (P=0.084). Ultimately, 3 of the 14 RRD eyes (21.4%), representing 1.2% of the total surgical cohort, lost 3 or more lines of vision compared to baseline.

Conclusion

PPV for symptomatic floaters is associated with a small risk of postoperative RRD. All eyes were successfully reattached with 1.2% experiencing a loss of 3 or more lines of vision.

records.title: COMPARISON OF TRACTION FORCES IN EX VIVO VITRECTOMY USING 25+®G 20K CPM DUAL-BLADE AND 25+®G 10K CPM SINGLE-BLADE VITRECTOMY PROBES.

content.title: COMPARISON OF TRACTION FORCES IN EX VIVO VITRECTOMY USING 25+®G 20K CPM DUAL-BLADE AND 25+®G 10K CPM SINGLE-BLADE VITRECTOMY PROBES.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To compare vitreous traction forces generated by a 25+® gauge (G) 20,000 cuts per minute (CPM) dual-blade vitrectomy probe (HYPERVIT®) and a 25+®G 10,000 CPM single-blade vitrectomy probe (Advanced ULTRAVIT®) under flow-matched conditions.

Methods

Bovine vitreous was used in a simulated ex vivo vitrectomy model. Each probe (n=10 per type) engaged vitreous within a balanced salt solution (BSS®) chamber, while a force sensor recorded traction forces. Vacuum levels were set at 260 mmHg (dual-blade) and 340 mmHg (single-blade) to achieve flow-matching, and traction forces were measured across percentiles.

Results

Under flow-matched conditions, the dual-blade probe exhibited lower traction forces. Excluding forces <0.5 millinewton (mN), the 90th, 95th, and 99th percentile forces were 12.8%, 14.4%, and 14.4% lower, respectively (p<0.05). Overall mean, mean peak, and mean maximum forces were lowered by 8.01%, 15.78%, and 12.22%, respectively (p<0.05). The single-blade probe recorded traction forces of 1.60 ± 0.07 mN, 2.93 ± 0.14 mN, and 6.97 ± 0.38 mN, respectively. Whereas the dual-blade probe showed 1.47 ± 0.04 mN, 2.46 ± 0.12 mN, and 6.12 ± 0.26 mN (p<0.05).

Conclusion

The 25+G 20K CPM dual-blade probe generated lower traction forces than the 25+G 10K CPM single-blade probe under flow-matched conditions.

records.title: Regional and Temporal Changes in Choroidal Vascularity after Panretinal Photocoagulation in Diabetic Retinopathy: A Widefield SS-OCTA Study.

content.title: Regional and Temporal Changes in Choroidal Vascularity after Panretinal Photocoagulation in Diabetic Retinopathy: A Widefield SS-OCTA Study.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To investigate the changes in choroidal vasculature after panretinal photocoagulation (PRP) in patients with proliferative diabetic retinopathy (PDR) using widefield swept-source optical coherence tomography angiography (SS-OCTA).

Methods

Thirty eyes of 30 PDR patients were enrolled and underwent SS-OCTA examination before PRP, and at 1 month and 3 months after PRP. Twenty-two age-matched healthy volunteers served as controls. Choroidal thickness (ChT), choroidal vascular volume (CVV), choroidal vascularity index (CVI), choroidal stromal volume (CSV), choriocapillaris flow deficit percentage (CC FD%), and central macular thickness (CMT) were automatically measured within concentric rings of 2.5, 5, 12, and 19 mm centered on the fovea.

Results

Post-PRP choroidal changes showed distinct regional specificity and time dependence. In the periphery (12-19 mm): CVV decreased (-5.45% at 1 month, P=0.045; -8.23% at 3 months, P<0.001); CC FD% increased (+48.9% at 1 month, +80.7% at 3 months, both P<0.001); CVI decreased only at 3 months (-3.57%, P=0.011); CSV remained unchanged. In the central region (0-2.5 mm): except for a mild decrease in CVV at 3 months (-4.01%, P=0.009), all other parameters showed no significant changes. CMT progressively increased (+7.49 7.50% at 1 month, +12.32% at 3 months, both P<0.01). Exploratory analysis showed that centralΔCVV was independently positively correlated withΔCMT (β=0.219P=0.002) Exploratory regression analysis showed that baseline CMT and central ΔCVV were independently associated with ΔCMT (β=0.352, P=0.041; B=528.414, P=0.002, respectively).

Conclusion

PRP induces "vessel-first atrophy" in the periphery with relative central preservation, supporting hemodynamic redistribution. Widefield SS-OCTA effectively evaluates post-PRP choroidal changes. The association between central choroidal vascular volume change and macular edema requires further investigation.

records.title: EVALUATING CLINICAL OUTCOMES OF AMNIOTIC MEMBRANE COVERAGE COMBINED WITH EARLY VITRECTOMY IN THE MANAGEMENT OF PERFORATING GLOBE INJURIES.

content.title: EVALUATING CLINICAL OUTCOMES OF AMNIOTIC MEMBRANE COVERAGE COMBINED WITH EARLY VITRECTOMY IN THE MANAGEMENT OF PERFORATING GLOBE INJURIES.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To evaluate the anatomical and functional outcomes of a surgical approach combining amniotic membrane coverage with early vitrectomy under low perfusion pressure in patients with perforating globe injuries.

Methods

The study involved 19 patients who presented with Zone 3 exit wounds of globe injuries. The surgical procedures included the administration of recombinant tissue plasminogen activator for hemorrhage clearance, pars plana vitrectomy, internal limiting membrane peeling or retinectomy depending on the presence of proliferative vitreoretinopathy, application of amniotic membrane over the exit wound, and intraocular tamponade injection. The postoperative follow-up period extended over 6 months.

Results

Anatomical success, defined as retinal reattachment, was achieved in 89.5% of cases, with a 100% rate of globe survival. The incidence of postoperative proliferative vitreoretinopathy was 10.5%. Best-corrected visual acuity improved in 89.47% of patients.

Conclusion

The combination of amniotic membrane coverage with early vitrectomy in the management of perforating globe injuries was associated with favorable anatomical outcomes, a low rate of postoperative proliferative vitreoretinopathy, and visual improvement in most patients. This approach represents a viable strategy for addressing the complex challenges in these severe ocular injuries.

records.title: SEVERE RETINAL NONPERFUSION IS ASSOCIATED WITH FEWER RETINAL LESIONS ON ULTRAWIDE-FIELD FUNDUS PHOTOGRAPHY IN PROLIFERATIVE DIABETIC RETINOPATHY.

content.title: SEVERE RETINAL NONPERFUSION IS ASSOCIATED WITH FEWER RETINAL LESIONS ON ULTRAWIDE-FIELD FUNDUS PHOTOGRAPHY IN PROLIFERATIVE DIABETIC RETINOPATHY.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To explore the relationship between the number of retinal lesions observed on ultrawide-field fundus photography (UWF-FP) and the nonperfusion index (NPI) quantified on UWF fluorescein angiography in patients with proliferative diabetic retinopathy (PDR).

Methods

The NPI was measured on early-phase UWF fluorescein angiography in 100 eyes from 100 patients with PDR, including both type 1 and type 2 diabetes. Eyes were divided into quartiles based on NPI values. Red dots (microaneurysms, retinal hemorrhages, and intraretinal microvascular abnormalities), venous beading, cotton-wool spots, and white thread-like arterioles were counted on UWF-FP.

Results

The mean NPI values for quartiles one to four were 2.8 ± 1.1%, 8.5 ± 2.1%, 17.3 ± 4.5%, and 42.8 ± 12.2%, respectively. Eyes in the highest NPI quartile (quartile 4) had significantly fewer retinal lesions on UWF-FP (76.1 ± 50.6) and fewer cotton-wool spots compared with those in the lowest NPI quartile, which showed 253.0 ± 165.5 retinal lesions ( P < 0.001). White thread-like arterioles were present in 80.0% of eyes in quartile four and none in quartile 1. Patients in quartile four were predominantly type 2 diabetics with higher rates of end-stage kidney disease, peripheral neuropathy, lower-extremity peripheral artery disease, and prior limb amputation or revascularization.

Conclusion

In patients with poorly controlled, long-standing type 2 diabetes complicated by renal failure, peripheral neuropathy, peripheral arterial disease, or lower-limb amputation, fluorescein angiography should be considered when highly ischemic PDR is suspected, particularly in the presence of white thread-like arterioles, as it may otherwise appear milder on color fundus photography.

records.title: Exploration of Potential Associations Between Sulfated Polysaccharide Exposure and Retinal Findings.

content.title: Exploration of Potential Associations Between Sulfated Polysaccharide Exposure and Retinal Findings.
content.abstract:
Purpose

Pentosan polysulfate sodium (PPS), a widely used treatment for interstitial cystitis, has been linked to a distinctive macular toxicity. A recent case report described a similar phenotype with fondaparinux, a related sulfated polysaccharide, raising the possibility of a broader class effect. We explored potential associations between exposure to non-PPS sulfated polysaccharides and retinal imaging findings resembling PPS maculopathy.

Methods

We conducted a single center retrospective study from 2018-2024. Emory Healthcare electronic health records were queried for adults with exposure to fondaparinux, enoxaparin, chondroitin containing products, alginate containing products, and/or dalteparin. Macular imaging during the study period was required for inclusion. A retina specialist reviewed macular imaging for features resembling PPS maculopathy. Given the high number of enoxaparin users with short exposure durations, imaging review for this group was limited to >1 year of documented exposure.

Results

A total of 218 patients were evaluated, including patients exposed to alginate (n = 12), fondaparinux (n = 25), chondroitin sulfate (n = 111), and enoxaparin (n = 70). Mean age at first qualifying macular imaging was 67.4 years and 59.5% were women. There were no cases resembling classic PPS maculopathy. Some patients did exhibit subtle macular pigment alterations without a clear diagnosis [fondaparinux 1 (4.0%); chondroitin sulfate 3 (2.7%); alginate 1 (8.3%)].

Conclusions

This study did not identify a relationship between non-PPS sulfated polysaccharide exposure and the development of macular disease resembling classic PPS maculopathy. Larger studies with increased power may be warranted to determine whether a rare association may be present.

records.title: Post-Pars Plana Vitrectomy Endophthalmitis in Patients with and without Systemic Immunosuppression.

content.title: Post-Pars Plana Vitrectomy Endophthalmitis in Patients with and without Systemic Immunosuppression.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To determine whether systemic immunosuppression is associated with endophthalmitis after pars plana vitrectomy (PPV), and whether risk varies by drug class and time window.

Methods

Retrospective propensity score matched cohort study using TriNetX, a federated network of 72 US healthcare organizations. Exposed adults undergoing PPV used corticosteroids, classic nonbiologic immunosuppressants, targeted small molecule immunomodulators, or biologics for at least 3 months before surgery; controls had none in the prior year. Matching controlled for demographics, comorbidities, and surgical indication. The outcome was endophthalmitis within 365 days, assessed over early (1-42 days), 1-90 day, and later (43-365 day) windows. Cox modeling was secondary.

Results

After matching, 25,997 patients per cohort were analyzed. No class was associated with endophthalmitis during the early window. During the later window, risk was higher for all immunosuppressants (RR 1.74; 95% CI 1.33 to 2.28; P < .0001), corticosteroids (RR 1.81; 95% CI 1.38 to 2.37; P < .0001), and biologics (RR 2.00; 95% CI 1.00 to 4.03; P = .045). In Cox regression, corticosteroids (HR 1.19; 95% CI 1.01 to 1.39; P = .037) and biologics (HR 1.51; 95% CI 1.08 to 2.11; P = .016) remained independent risk factors.

Conclusion

Systemic corticosteroid use prior to PPV was associated with late-onset endophthalmitis, with excess risk appearing between 43 and 365 days rather than in the early period. This timing is atypical for surgically acquired infection, and some late events may reflect endogenous or inflammatory disease. Immunosuppressed patients may warrant a longer window of suspicion.

records.title: PROGNOSTIC FACTORS FOR CLINICAL OUTCOMES AND LESION REACTIVATION IN STAGE 2 to 3 TYPE 3 MACULAR NEOVASCULARIZATION TREATED USING a TREAT-AND-EXTEND REGIMEN.

content.title: PROGNOSTIC FACTORS FOR CLINICAL OUTCOMES AND LESION REACTIVATION IN STAGE 2 to 3 TYPE 3 MACULAR NEOVASCULARIZATION TREATED USING a TREAT-AND-EXTEND REGIMEN.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To evaluate the treatment outcomes of Type 3 macular neovascularization and identify factors associated with visual outcomes and lesion reactivation during 76 weeks of aflibercept therapy using a treat-and-extend (TAE) regimen.

Methods

This post hoc analysis included 25 treatment-naive patients with Stage 2 to 3 Type 3 macular neovascularization who participated in a previous prospective study and received aflibercept treatment for 76 weeks using a TAE regimen. The incidence and outcomes of the first lesion reactivation were assessed. Factors associated with lesion reactivation and best-corrected visual acuity at the final visit were evaluated.

Results

Lesion reactivation occurred in 8 patients (32.0%) during the treatment period; however, no patient experienced a loss of ≥5 letters before or after the first reactivation. In multivariate analysis, best-corrected visual acuity at Week 16 was a strong predictor of final best-corrected visual acuity ( P < 0.001, β = 1.191), and older age was significantly associated with a lower risk of lesion reactivation ( P = 0.036, β = 0.811).

Conclusion

Early visual outcomes after the initial loading injections can serve as reliable prognostic indicators for long-term treatment of Stage 2 to 3 Type 3 macular neovascularization using a TAE regimen. In younger patients, the increased likelihood of lesion reactivation should be considered. Although lesion reactivation occurred in approximately one third of the patients, it did not result in significant visual deterioration. Further studies analyzing treatment outcomes in Stage 1 disease are required.

records.title: ULTRAWIDE-FIELD COLOR FUNDUS IMAGES AND ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE FOR DIAGNOSIS OF DIABETIC RETINOPATHY: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.

content.title: ULTRAWIDE-FIELD COLOR FUNDUS IMAGES AND ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE FOR DIAGNOSIS OF DIABETIC RETINOPATHY: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
content.abstract:
Purpose

Ultrawide-field (UWF) fundus cameras capture a larger retinal area without pupil dilation. The authors summarized evidence and diagnostic performance of artificial intelligence (AI)-driven diabetic retinopathy (DR) assessments using UWF images (UWFIs).

Methods

The authors searched PubMed, Scopus, the Cochrane Library, and Web of Science to February 9, 2025, for studies evaluating DR using UWFIs and AI analyses. They followed the PRISMA guidelines and assessed study quality using the Joanna Briggs Institute Critical Appraisal Checklist for diagnostic accuracy. Forest plots and summary receiver operating characteristic curves estimated sensitivity and specificity of AI-driven DR screening using UWFI.

Results

Of 527 records identified, 17 studies were included in the systematic review and four in the meta-analysis. All studies used Optos software. Among the included studies, two evaluated DR discrimination from multiple retinal disorders, six addressed DR stage classification based on guideline scales, six evaluated DR screening, and one each focused on referable retinal pathology detection, DR progression prediction, and detection of clinical DR features. The summary sensitivity, specificity, and area under receiver operating characteristic curve for AI-driven DR screening using UWFI were 85.0%, 72.5%, and 0.870 (0.838-0.897), respectively. UWFI-based AI screening showed acceptable sensitivity but limited specificity.

Conclusion

AI-driven DR screening using UWFIs may achieve acceptable sensitivity but with limited specificity; however, these findings should be interpreted with caution, given the limited number of available studies. Further studies using larger, diverse data sets with rigorous external validation across UWF platforms are needed to improve generalizability and clarify the clinical role of UWFI-based AI.

records.title: THE IMPACT OF THE ECTOPIC INNER FOVEAL LAYER WITH PRESERVED FOVEAL CONTOUR ON RETINAL MICROVASCULATURE CHANGES AFTER EPIRETINAL MEMBRANE REMOVAL.

content.title: THE IMPACT OF THE ECTOPIC INNER FOVEAL LAYER WITH PRESERVED FOVEAL CONTOUR ON RETINAL MICROVASCULATURE CHANGES AFTER EPIRETINAL MEMBRANE REMOVAL.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To evaluate the long-term effects of preoperative ectopic inner foveal layer (EIFL) with preserved foveal contour on postoperative retinal microvascular changes in patients with epiretinal membrane.

Methods

Patients were divided into two groups based on EIFL presence: Group 1 without EIFL and Group 2 with EIFL. Superficial and deep vessel densities (SVDs and DVDs), corresponding to the superficial and deep vascular complexes, were quantitatively assessed using OCT angiography.

Results

The SVDs at baseline, 1, 3, 6, and 12 months were 27.9 ± 7.7, 27.6 ± 8.3, 25.9 ± 7.8, 26.1 ± 7.0, and 24.9 ± 8.0% in Group 1, respectively ( P = 0.075), and 31.6 ± 7.3, 28.0 ± 6.3, 26.7 ± 5.6, 25.4 ± 5.7, and 22.9 ± 5.6% in Group 2, respectively ( P < 0.001). The DVDs were 21.9 ± 4.6, 22.9 ± 4.5, 23.6 ± 5.1, 24.2 ± 4.0, and 23.6 ± 4.7% in Group 1, respectively ( P = 0.277), and 20.6 ± 4.7, 22.8 ± 4.2, 23.2 ± 3.7, 23.6 ± 5.0, and 23.4 ± 3.8% in Group 2, respectively ( P = 0.003). In the multivariable analysis, baseline BCVA was significantly associated with changes in BCVA in Group 1, whereas in Group 2, baseline BCVA and DVD showed significant associations with BCVA changes.

Conclusion

Patients with EIFL and preserved foveal contour demonstrated more prominent alterations in retinal microvasculature after surgery, and these changes, especially within the deep vascular complex, are considered to play an important role in visual improvement.

records.title: 3D corneal and retinal bioprinting: Tissue engineering strategies, translational challenges, and clinical opportunities.
records.publisher: Progress in retinal and eye research

content.title: 3D corneal and retinal bioprinting: Tissue engineering strategies, translational challenges, and clinical opportunities.
content.abstract: Three-dimensional bioprinting has emerged as a promising strategy for addressing major unmet needs in ophthalmology, including the global shortage of donor corneal tissue and the absence of restorative therapies for retinal degenerative disease. Advances in biomaterials, stem cell biology, and biofabrication have enabled increasingly sophisticated ocular constructs, ranging from engineered corneal grafts to multicellular retinal models that recapitulate key aspects of native tissue architecture. However, substantial challenges remain in reproducing the optical, mechanical, and biological functions required for clinical translation. This review critically evaluates the current state of corneal and retinal bioprinting through a framework organized around tissue target, fabrication modality, and intended application. Major bioprinting approaches, including extrusion-based, laser-assisted, drop-on-demand, and light-based technologies, are compared with respect to resolution, cell compatibility, scalability, and translational potential. Particular emphasis is placed on the engineering constraints governing construct fidelity, bioink design, tissue integration, and long-term functional performance. Current evidence suggests that corneal and retinal bioprinting have progressed along distinct translational trajectories. Corneal bioprinting has achieved encouraging preclinical outcomes, with one approach entering early clinical evaluation, whereas retinal bioprinting has generated highly informative disease models but remains at an earlier stage of translational development. Across both tissues, the field has increasingly shifted from reproducing individual cellular components toward reconstructing the biological interfaces and multicellular systems that underlie tissue function. Future progress will depend on establishing functional validation frameworks, reproducible manufacturing workflows, and standardized benchmarks to support the clinical development of vision-restoring bioprinted constructs.

records.title: Impact of posterior vitreous detachment on clinical outcomes in eyes with branch retinal vein occlusion.

content.title: Impact of posterior vitreous detachment on clinical outcomes in eyes with branch retinal vein occlusion.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To investigate posterior vitreous detachment (PVD) status in eyes with branch retinal vein occlusion (BRVO) and its relationship to structural and treatment outcomes.

Methods

Retrospective cohort study of eyes with treatment-naïve BRVO diagnosed within one year of onset from 2009 through 2021, with at least one year of follow-up. Eyes were stratified by PVD status on optical coherence tomography at presentation. Outcomes included cystoid macular edema (CME) prevalence, central subfield thickness (CST), and number of intravitreal injections.

Results

Of 88 eyes, 33 (37.5%) had complete PVD and 55 (62.5%) did not. Patients with complete PVD were older (median 75 vs 67 years; p=0.02) and had a lower prevalence of hypertension (66.7% vs 89.1%; p=0.01). At one year, CME was less frequent in eyes with complete PVD (65.6% vs 88.9%; p=0.01), after adjustments for hypertension, baseline CME, and CST. Eyes with complete PVD had lower median CST (277.5 vs 301.0 μm; p=0.045) and required fewer median injections (4.0 vs 7.0; p=0.01) at one year, after adjustments for baseline CME and CST, but not hypertension. A significant interaction between baseline CST and PVD status was observed for one-year injection burden (p=0.03), with complete PVD associated with fewer injections at lower CST, but more injections at higher CST.

Conclusion

In eyes with BRVO, complete PVD at presentation was associated with lower one-year CME prevalence, CST, and injection burden. The relationship between PVD status and injection burden varied by baseline CST, suggesting PVD status and CST may provide complementary information regarding treatment burden.

records.title: Lichen Simplex Chronicus is Associated with an Increased Risk of Rhegmatogenous Retinal Detachment and Retinal Tears: A Propensity Score-Matched Cohort Study.

content.title: Lichen Simplex Chronicus is Associated with an Increased Risk of Rhegmatogenous Retinal Detachment and Retinal Tears: A Propensity Score-Matched Cohort Study.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To determine whether lichen simplex chronicus (LSC) is associated with an increased risk of rhegmatogenous retinal detachment (RRD) and retinal tears without detachment (RT) compared with adults without LSC.

Methods

This retrospective propensity score-matched cohort study used TriNetX to compare adults (≥18 years) with LSC to matched adults without LSC. Patients with prior RRD, RT, ocular trauma, or proliferative diabetic retinopathy were excluded. Propensity score matching (1:1) was performed on demographics, ocular and systemic comorbidities, and prior ophthalmology encounters. Incidence of RRD, RT, the composite endpoint of RRD or RT (RRD/RT), retinopexy, RRD repair, and the composite of RRD repair or retinopexy were compared using risk analysis and Kaplan-Meier survival analysis with Cox regression, yielding risk ratios (RR) and hazard ratios (HR) with 95% confidence intervals (CI).

Results

After 1:1 propensity score matching, the study included 64,170 patients per group. LSC patients had significantly higher rates of RRD (RR 8.83, 95% CI 4.86-16.05; p<0.001), RT (RR 10.15, 95% CI 6.79-15.19; p<0.001), and composite RRD/RT (RR 9.60, 95% CI 6.78-13.60; p<0.001). On procedure analysis, retinopexy (RR 6.64, 95% CI 3.52-12.51; p<0.001), RRD repair (RR 4.07, 95% CI 2.27-7.31; p<0.001), and the composite of retinopexy or RRD repair (RR 5.08, 95% CI 3.28-7.87; p<0.001) occurred more frequently in the LSC cohort.

Conclusion

LSC is associated with a substantially increased risk of incident diagnosis of RRD, RT, composite RRD/RT, and their procedural repair after adjustment for known risk factors. These findings suggest LSC may increase the risk of rhegmatogenous retinal pathology.

records.title: Retinal Structure Reflects Cumulative Blast Exposure and Blast-Related Mild Traumatic Brain Injury.

content.title: Retinal Structure Reflects Cumulative Blast Exposure and Blast-Related Mild Traumatic Brain Injury.
content.abstract: U.S. military service members experienced a high rate of blast exposures during post-9/11 military conflicts. Though a growing body of literature suggests that these exposures have long term consequences for health, objective biomarkers of blast-related neurotrauma remain limited. We used optical coherence tomography (OCT) to determine whether blast-related mild traumatic brain injury (mTBI) and cumulative blast exposure burden were associated with retinal microstructural changes. A retrospective, cross-sectional cohort study at VA Boston Healthcare System. Seventy-three United States post 9/11 veterans enrolled in the Translational Research Center for TBI & Stress Disorders (TRACTS) longitudinal cohort study who underwent OCT imaging based on assessment availability. Principal observations were blast-related mild traumatic brain injury and cumulative lifetime blast exposure burden. Retinal thickness as measured by high-resolution Spectralis OCT imaging, including 7 individual macular layers, combined macular layers (inner retina, outer retina, and total retina), and the peripapillary retinal nerve fiber layer, using automated segmentation software. Among 73 participants (mean [SD] age, 40.8 [9.4] years; 63 [86%] male), 25 had a history of blast mTBI (blast mTBI+) and 48 did not (blast mTBI-). Participants with blast mTBI+ had significantly thicker retinal layers in the macula, specifically in the 3mm quadrants around the fovea. The peripapillary RNFL (pRNFL) was significantly thinner in the blast mTBI+ group (p = .009), with the most significant thinning occurring nasally, most notably superior/nasal (p < .001). Greater cumulative blast exposure burden was associated with lower pRNFL thickness (ρ = -.288, p = .013) and greater macular outer retinal layer thickness (ρ = .319, p = .007). In cross-validated predictive analyses, pRNFL, outer plexiform layer, and outer retinal layer thickness significantly predicted cumulative blast exposure burden (leave-one-subject-out correlation, r = .335; conditional Monte Carlo permutation p = .005, full discovery Monte Carlo permutation p = .021). Retinal structural measures distinguished veterans with blast-related mild traumatic brain injury and predicted cumulative blast exposure burden. These findings support OCT as an accessible approach for identifying retinal biomarkers of blast-related neurotrauma and cumulative blast exposure.

records.title: Retinal phenotypes and longitudinal clinical courses in patients with NPHP1-associated Senior-Løken syndrome.

content.title: Retinal phenotypes and longitudinal clinical courses in patients with NPHP1-associated Senior-Løken syndrome.
content.abstract:
Purpose

This study aimed to describe retinal phenotype, longitudinal clinical course, and genetic findings in Japanese patients with NPHP1-associated Senior-Løken syndrome and their siblings.

Design

Retrospective, multicenter case series.

Patients and methods

This study included 12 patients with biallelic pathogenic NPHP1 variants, comprising 10 probands with symptomatic retinal dystrophy recruited from six ophthalmic centers across Japan and 2 affected siblings identified through family screening. Clinical and genetic findings were analyzed. Retinal dystrophy was diagnosed using fundus photography, fundus autofluorescence (FAF), optical coherence tomography, and electroretinography. Genetic testing was performed using whole-exome and/or whole-genome sequencing. Follow-up ranged from 0 to 44 years (mean, 14.6 years).

Main outcome measures

Retinal phenotype, onset of retinopathy and nephropathy, and genotype.

Results

Retinal phenotypes included cone/cone-rod dystrophy (4 patients), retinitis pigmentosa (4 patients), sector retinitis pigmentosa (2 patients), pigmented paravenous retinochoroidal atrophy (1 patient), and normal retina (1 patient). FAF images showed a descending tract in 5 patients. Retinopathy preceded nephropathy in 9 patients, all of whom were initially diagnosed with Leber congenital amaurosis or early-onset retinal dystrophy. Genetic testing showed that 11 patients harbored a homozygous whole-NPHP1 deletion, whereas 1 carried compound heterozygous NPHP1 and EYS variants.

Conclusions

Patients with NPHP1-associated Senior-Løken syndrome showed considerable inter- and intrafamilial variability in retinal phenotype. Pigmented paravenous retinochoroidal atrophy can be associated with NPHP1 variants. A descending tract on FAF imaging may be a characteristic feature of retinal degeneration in Senior-Løken syndrome. Retinopathy, which commonly manifests as Leber congenital amaurosis or early-onset retinal dystrophy, often precedes nephropathy in patients with NPHP1-associated Senior-Løken syndrome.

records.title: EFFICACY AND SAFETY OF SUBTHRESHOLD LASER IN PATIENTS WITH ACUTE CENTRAL SEROUS CHORIORETINOPATHY: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.

content.title: EFFICACY AND SAFETY OF SUBTHRESHOLD LASER IN PATIENTS WITH ACUTE CENTRAL SEROUS CHORIORETINOPATHY: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.
content.abstract:
Purpose

Subthreshold laser has been proposed as a potentially safer and more effective alternative for patients with acute central serous chorioretinopathy (CSC). Hence, the objective of this systematic review was to assess the efficacy and safety of subthreshold laser treatment for acute CSC.

Methods

We performed a comprehensive systematic search of PubMed/MEDLINE, EMBASE, and CENTRAL from their inception up to March 24, 2026. We included randomized controlled trials comparing the efficacy and/or safety of subthreshold laser against any comparator. Random-effects meta-analyses were conducted, and the certainty of evidence was rated using the minimally contextualized GRADE approach.

Results

Six randomized controlled trials (401 participants) in patients with acute CSC were included. Compared with conventional laser, subthreshold laser probably yields similar improvements in visual acuity and reduces retinal pigment epithelium damage but probably leads to a lower rate of subretinal fluid resolution. When compared with observation, subthreshold laser may result in similar visual acuity outcomes but may reduce persistent metamorphopsia and increase subretinal fluid resolution, although the certainty of evidence is very low. Compared with half-dose photodynamic therapy, subthreshold laser may provide comparable visual outcomes but lower anatomical improvement, with very low certainty of evidence.

Conclusion

In acute CSC, subthreshold laser appears safer than conventional laser and produces similar visual outcomes, although its anatomical efficacy is limited. Its potential advantages over observation or photodynamic therapy remain uncertain because of low-certainty evidence.

records.title: EFFECTIVENESS AND SAFETY OF BIOSIMILAR ANTIVASCULAR ENDOTHELIAL GROWTH FACTOR FOR RETINAL DISEASES: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.

content.title: EFFECTIVENESS AND SAFETY OF BIOSIMILAR ANTIVASCULAR ENDOTHELIAL GROWTH FACTOR FOR RETINAL DISEASES: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To evaluate the comparative effectiveness and safety of biosimilar antivascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) versus reference anti-VEGF intravitreal injections for the treatment of retinal diseases.

Methods

A systematic review and meta-analysis was performed on studies identified through searches of Ovid MEDLINE, Embase, and the Cochrane Library between January 2015 and September 2024. Studies evaluating effectiveness and/or safety outcomes of biosimilar anti-VEGF were included. Meta-analysis was performed with a random-effects model. Risk of bias assessment was performed with the Joanna Briggs Institute tools, and certainty of evidence was evaluated with the Grading of Recommendations, Assessment, Development, and Evaluation criteria.

Results

A total of 25 studies were included in the meta-analysis. Diagnoses studied were neovascular age-related macular degeneration, diabetic macular edema, retinal vein occlusion, and polypoidal choroidal vasculopathy. There were no significant differences in final visual acuity, change in visual acuity, final retinal thickness, change in retinal thickness, and incidence of adverse events over a follow-up duration of 12 to 63.6 weeks. Subgroup analyses of randomized controlled trials, observational studies, age-related macular degeneration, diabetic macular edema, and agent-specific analysis (aflibercept and ranibizumab) were not significant. Findings are supported by evidence of moderate to high certainty as per the Grading of Recommendations, Assessment, Development, and Evaluation tool. There was a low to moderate risk of bias in the included study as per the Joanna Briggs Institute tools.

Conclusion

Biosimilar anti-VEGF is comparable with reference anti-VEGF regarding safety profile and visual outcomes. Future research should prioritize including diverse patient populations and adopting standardized, extended follow-up periods to enhance the assessment of long-term safety and effectiveness of biosimilars.

records.title: SILICONE OIL MIGRATION DURING INTRAVITREAL ANTI-VASCULAR ENDOTHELIAL GROWTH FACTOR INJECTIONS: A Review of Clinical Evidence and Factors Related to Transmission.

content.title: SILICONE OIL MIGRATION DURING INTRAVITREAL ANTI-VASCULAR ENDOTHELIAL GROWTH FACTOR INJECTIONS: A Review of Clinical Evidence and Factors Related to Transmission.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To evaluate the incidence, mechanisms, and clinical implications of silicone oil droplet transmission during intravitreal anti-vascular endothelial growth factor injections and to review strategies to mitigate contamination risks.

Methods

A systematic review of observational and review studies from PubMed and MEDLINE was conducted, focusing on incidence, contributing factors, and clinical outcomes of silicone oil contamination during IVIs. Specific attention was given to syringe design, storage conditions, variations among anti-vascular endothelial growth factor agents, and injection techniques.

Results

The review found that prevalence is high in chronically injected eyes, although per-injection rates are low, often clustering because of syringe batches or techniques. Contributing factors include freeze-thaw cycles, mechanical agitation, spray-siliconized low dead space syringes, and improper plunger handling, which can lead to asymptomatic droplets or symptomatic floaters. No severe complications such as endophthalmitis were reported. Hypotheses link silicone oil to ocular hypertension or inflammation via trabecular obstruction or immunogenic responses, but the reviewed studies show no direct evidence. Mitigation involves the use of silicone-free/prefilled syringes, strict storage, gentle handling, and refined techniques such as priming and smooth plunger depression.

Conclusion

Silicone oil contamination during IVIs can be minimized through careful optimization of syringe design, handling practices, and injection techniques. Embracing silicone-free or low-silicone syringe systems, alongside meticulous procedural protocols, offers the potential to enhance the safety and clinical outcomes of intravitreal anti-vascular endothelial growth factor therapy.

records.title: THERAPEUTICS FOR MANAGEMENT OF PROLIFERATIVE VITREORETINOPATHY RELATED TO RHEGMATOGENOUS RETINAL DETACHMENT: A Network Meta-Analysis.

content.title: THERAPEUTICS FOR MANAGEMENT OF PROLIFERATIVE VITREORETINOPATHY RELATED TO RHEGMATOGENOUS RETINAL DETACHMENT: A Network Meta-Analysis.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To compare the efficacy and safety of adjunctive therapies for proliferative vitreoretinopathy (PVR) related to rhegmatogenous retinal detachment (RRD).

Methods

A systematic literature search was conducted on Ovid MEDLINE, Embase, and the Cochrane Library for randomized controlled trials (RCTs) from January 2000 to December 2025. A Bayesian random-effects network meta-analysis was used to compare different therapies.

Results

A total of 2,519 patients from 18 RCTs were included (1,339 receiving adjunctive treatments and 1,180 receiving placebo). Oral retinoic acid was associated with significantly higher primary (hazard ratio [HR] = 2.86, 95% CI = [1.16, 7.53]) and final (HR = 2.90, 95% CI = [1.12, 7.50]) retinal reattachment rates, improved visual acuity (MD=-0.89, 95% CI = [-1.68, -0.08]), and a lower incidence of postoperative macular pucker (HR = 0.12, 95% CI = [0.02, 0.50]) compared with placebo. Oral prednisolone had a lower rate of PVR recurrence compared with placebo (HR = 0.37, 95% CI = [0.17, 0.79]), while oral retinoic acid (HR = 0.06, 95% CI = [0.00, 0.50]) and intravitreal dexamethasone (HR = 0.23, 95% CI = [0.05, 0.81]) were associated with reduced rates of RRD reoperation.

Conclusion

Oral retinoic acid ranked highest for primary outcomes in PVR associated with RRD; however, this finding was driven by a single RCT with limited sample size. Oral prednisolone reduced PVR recurrence, while intravitreal dexamethasone lowered reoperation risk, compared with placebo.

records.title: COMPARABLE RESULTS OF SUBRETINAL INJECTION AND INTRAVITREAL INJECTION OF TISSUE PLASMINOGEN ACTIVATOR IN THE TREATMENT OF SUBMACULAR HEMORRHAGE: A Meta-Analysis of Efficacy.

content.title: COMPARABLE RESULTS OF SUBRETINAL INJECTION AND INTRAVITREAL INJECTION OF TISSUE PLASMINOGEN ACTIVATOR IN THE TREATMENT OF SUBMACULAR HEMORRHAGE: A Meta-Analysis of Efficacy.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To estimate the efficacy of intravitreal injection (IVI) versus subretinal injection (SRI) of tissue plasminogen activator in the treatment of submacular hemorrhage (SMH).

Methods

A comprehensive literature search was conducted in six major data sets from inception to 31 October 2025. Random effects meta-analysis was performed to evaluate the final best-corrected visual acuity (BCVA, logMAR) and the changes in central retinal thickness (CRT, μm), and the risk ratio of complete displacement of hemorrhage.

Results

A total of seven studies on 353 eyes were finally included. Best-corrected visual acuity was similar between the IVI and SRI groups at 1 month and 6 months postoperation, while better in the IVI group 3 months postoperatively. The final CRT was similar between the two groups. There were no statistical differences between the two groups in the RRs of complete displacement of hemorrhage, total adverse events, recurrent SMH, increased intraocular pressure, postoperative retinal detachment, and vitreous hemorrhages.

Conclusion

The IVI group showed a better BCVA at 3 months, the two groups showed comparable results in the recovery of BCVA, CRT, and complete hemorrhage displacement at the final visit (within 6 months).

records.title: Prevalence, Ocular Manifestations, and Treatment Response in Postbariatric Vitamin A Deficiency: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.

content.title: Prevalence, Ocular Manifestations, and Treatment Response in Postbariatric Vitamin A Deficiency: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
content.abstract:
Topic

To estimate procedure-specific prevalence of biochemical vitamin A deficiency after bariatric surgery and synthesize ocular manifestations, postoperative latency, and response to vitamin A repletion.

Clinical relevance

As bariatric surgery volume continues to rise, recognition of procedure-specific vitamin A deficiency and its ocular manifestations may improve ophthalmic surveillance, earlier diagnosis, and timely repletion in postbariatric patients.

Methods

Following PROSPERO registration (CRD420261329094), we did a systematic review of MEDLINE, Embase, the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials, Scopus, and Web of Science through March 2026 for studies reporting vitamin A status or ocular manifestations after bariatric surgery. Risk of bias was evaluated with the Cochrane RoB 2, Risk of Bias in Nonrandomized Studies of Interventions, and Joanna Briggs Institute checklists; the overall certainty of evidence was assessed with the Grading of Recommendations, Assessment, Development, and Evaluation framework.

Results

Of 1574 abstracts screened, 27 reports representing 21 unique studies met inclusion criteria; 18 contributed quantitative data, of which 9 nonpregnancy surveillance cohorts (455 tested participants) entered the prevalence meta-analysis. Prevalence was 18.0% after Roux-en-Y gastric bypass (RYGB), 59.0% after biliopancreatic diversion (BPD), 37.8% after BPD with duodenal switch, and 42.5% after jejunoileal bypass; the pooled estimate across these heterogeneous procedures and study-defined retinol thresholds was 26.1% (95% CI, 18.5-35.4), reported as a secondary summary. Pregnancy-specific post-RYGB prevalence was 63.3% (95% CI, 43.9-80.1). Night blindness prevalence was 60.1% in active/formal nonoverlapping cohorts with symptom denominators. Median latency to ocular presentation was 5 years after RYGB and 14 to 27 years after BPD with duodenal switch, jejunoileal bypass, or revisional procedures (19 patients). Among 14 postbariatric treatment-response records with assessable ocular outcomes, 13 (93%) improved or resolved.

Conclusion

Among the procedures with adequate data, vitamin A deficiency is procedure-specific and common during pregnancy after RYGB. Ocular disease may present years to decades after surgery but often improves when deficiency is recognized and treated. Certainty was limited by heterogeneity, the small number of cohorts for some procedure subgroups, and selective reporting of ocular outcomes. Nyctalopia, ocular surface disease, atypical outer retinal findings, or unexplained visual decline in a postbariatric patient warrant serum retinol testing.

records.title: SURGICAL OUTCOMES OF LAMELLAR MACULAR HOLE EYES WITH OR WITHOUT PRESERVATION OF LAMELLAR HOLE-ASSOCIATED EPIRETINAL PROLIFERATION TECHNIQUE: A Meta-analysis.

content.title: SURGICAL OUTCOMES OF LAMELLAR MACULAR HOLE EYES WITH OR WITHOUT PRESERVATION OF LAMELLAR HOLE-ASSOCIATED EPIRETINAL PROLIFERATION TECHNIQUE: A Meta-analysis.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To evaluate sparing or embedding technique for lamellar hole-associated epiretinal proliferation and in comparison with traditional internal limiting membrane and epiretinal membrane peeling in lamellar macular holes.

Methods

PubMed, Web of Science, Medline, EMBASE, Cochrane, CNKI, Wan Fang, and VIP Databases (PROSPERO number CRD42024466392) were searched. Trials of various lamellar hole-associated epiretinal proliferation removal or preservation techniques in lamellar macular holes were included (case reports of only 1 case excluded). Postoperative changes in best-corrected visual acuity were calculated. Central retinal thickness and number of patients with new postoperative intact ellipsoid zones were secondary outcomes.

Results

Eight studies were eligible and four compared with peeling groups. Preservation groups showed a significant visual improvement operatively (mean difference = -0.25 logMAR; 95% confidence interval = -0.30 to -0.21; P < 0.00001) and improved compared with peeling groups (mean difference = -0.19 logMAR; 95% confidence interval = -0.29 to -0.1; P < 0.0001). In addition, the number of patients with intact ellipsoid zones increased in the preserving groups (odd ratio = 2.55; 95% confidence interval = 1.48-4.38; P = 0.0007) and also increased compared with peeling groups (odd ratio =10.80; 95% confidence interval = 1.86-62.83; P = 0.008).

Conclusion

Based on the current evidence, lamellar hole-associated epiretinal proliferation sparing or embedding technique has favorable postoperative outcomes compared with peeling technique for lamellar macular holes.

records.title: Clinical and Multimodal Imaging Findings in Extensive Macular Atrophy With Pseudodrusen (EMAP): A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.

content.title: Clinical and Multimodal Imaging Findings in Extensive Macular Atrophy With Pseudodrusen (EMAP): A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
content.abstract:
Topic

This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to integrate the clinical and multimodal imaging features of extensive macular atrophy associated with pseudodrusen (EMAP), and to evaluate its progression and associated risk factors.

Clinical relevance

EMAP is a retinal disorder with a distinct phenotype and poor visual prognosis that typically affects patients in their middle age. There is no standardized classification for EMAP nor a clear understanding of its etiology. Identifying clinical and imaging biomarkers is critical to improve EMAP diagnosis and guiding future research.

Methods

We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis following PRISMA guidelines (PROSPERO, CRD42024474924). A comprehensive literature search of MEDLINE, EMBASE, Web of Science, and ClinicalTrials.gov was performed up to June 19, 2025. Randomized and nonrandomized studies of EMAP were eligible. Meta-analyses were performed using random-effects models. Heterogeneity was assessed with the I2 statistic, and risk of bias by the NOS. The examined outcomes were disease symptoms, best-corrected visual acuity (BCVA), progression of macular atrophy, imaging biomarkers, and systemic associations. EMAP was diagnosed using multimodal imaging analysis.

Results

Sixteen studies met the inclusion criteria for qualitative analysis, and 12 datasets were included (N = 1096 eyes). The mean BCVA at diagnosis was 0.62 logMAR (95% CI: 0.47-0.76; I² = 95.6%), with a mean worsening of 0.41 logMAR (3 lines of vision) over 2.1 years. Disease progression involved an increase in the macular atrophy area by an average of 8.3 mm² over 3.9 years (95% CI: 3-3.57; I² = 69.8%). Optical coherence tomography showed a mean central choroidal thickness of 135.8 (95% CI: 113.3-158.3; I² = 94.4%). Electroretinography data indicated a rod dysfunction with abnormal photopic response. Rheumatic fever was reported in 89% of patients across Brazilian cohorts (95% CI: 83.2-93; I² = 0%).

Conclusions

This meta-analysis has limitations, mostly due to heterogeneity and biases inherent to non-randomized studies of this disease, hence the inconsistencies in the results and hypothesized associations underlying EMAP. Despite the different imaging modalities used to diagnose EMAP, the results demonstrate the common features that characterize and support its diagnosis.

records.title: Risk Factors for Retinal Pigment Epithelium Tears in Patients With Neovascular Age-Related Macular Degeneration: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.

content.title: Risk Factors for Retinal Pigment Epithelium Tears in Patients With Neovascular Age-Related Macular Degeneration: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
content.abstract:
Topic

To identify and synthesize clinical, imaging, and treatment-related risk factors associated with retinal pigment epithelium (RPE) tears in neovascular age-related macular degeneration (nAMD).

Clinical relevance

RPE tears are a vision-threatening complication of nAMD, occurring most often in eyes with pigment epithelial detachments (PEDs) and frequently temporally associated with initiation of antivascular endothelial growth factor therapy. Improved recognition of high-risk PED features may enhance counseling and risk stratification.

Methods

This systematic review and meta-analysis followed Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses guidelines and was prospectively registered in PROSPERO (CRD420251075278). MEDLINE, Embase, and CENTRAL were searched from inception to December 15, 2025. Randomized and nonrandomized studies of adults (≥50 years) with nAMD evaluating candidate predictors of RPE tear were included. Two reviewers independently screened, extracted data, and assessed risk of bias (RoB 2, ROBINS-I). Random-effects meta-analyses were performed for baseline PED height and area, with per-study weighting, standardized mean difference (SMD), and leave-one-out sensitivity analyses. Certainty was assessed using Grading of Recommendations, Assessment, Development, and Evaluation.

Results

Sixteen studies comprising 4043 eyes were included. Five studies (55 tear eyes; 370 controls; 425 eyes) showed greater baseline PED height in eyes developing tears (mean difference [MD], 212.39 µm; 95% confidence interval [CI], 133.87-290.91; I² = 24.6%; SMD, 1.09). Four studies (48 tear eyes; 1312 controls; 1360 eyes) showed larger baseline PED area (MD, 5.80 mm²; 95% CI, 3.48-8.12; I² = 2.7%; SMD, 0.88). Both persisted across all leave-one-out iterations; omitting the study contributing 43.5% of the area weight increased the effect (MD, 7.11 mm²). Fibrovascular PED, greater basal diameter and volume, subretinal fluid, sub-RPE clefts, radial hyperreflective lines, and occult or hemorrhagic macular neovascularization were also associated with tears. Antivascular endothelial growth factor agent selection was not consistently associated. Most studies were at moderate to serious risk of bias; certainty was very low.

Conclusion

Baseline PED morphology, particularly increased height, is the most consistently reported association with RPE tear in nAMD. Because the evidence is predominantly retrospective, largely unadjusted, and of very low certainty, these are associations rather than validated predictive markers. Prospective studies using standardized imaging protocols are needed.

records.title: Anti-VEGF versus Laser Photocoagulation Surgery for Primary Treatment of Retinopathy of Prematurity: Neurodevelopmental Outcomes: A Report by the American Academy of Ophthalmology.

content.title: Anti-VEGF versus Laser Photocoagulation Surgery for Primary Treatment of Retinopathy of Prematurity: Neurodevelopmental Outcomes: A Report by the American Academy of Ophthalmology.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To review the evidence on neurodevelopmental outcomes after intravitreal anti-VEGF compared with laser photocoagulation surgery (LPC) for primary treatment of retinopathy of prematurity (ROP).

Methods

A literature search was last conducted in the PubMed database in December 2025 without date restrictions and limited to articles published in English. The search yielded 52 articles, 26 of which met criteria for inclusion. The panel methodologist assigned ratings to the articles according to the level of evidence.

Results

Of the 26 articles included, 4 articles on 3 randomized controlled trials (RCTs) were rated level II evidence and 22 comparative cohort studies were rated level III evidence. The studies included infants who were treated and followed over a 17-year period from 2006 through 2022 in 39 countries. The most common neurodevelopmental test used was the Bayley Scales of Infant and Toddler Development, used in 13 studies (50%). The age at assessment ranged from 0 months corrected age to 12 years, where most studies (n = 14 [54%]) included testing of infants younger than 24 months of age. Most studies (n = 20 [77%]), including all RCTs, did not detect a statistically significant difference in neurodevelopmental outcomes after anti-VEGF compared with LPC for primary treatment of ROP. Neurodevelopmental outcomes were found to be worse among those infants treated with intravitreal bevacizumab (IVB) for primary treatment in 4 studies and among those treated with LPC for primary treatment in 2 studies. Only 5 studies (19%) included intelligence quotient (IQ) testing beyond 4 years of age, and none detected a statistically significant difference in IQ between those who received anti-VEGF (IVB in 4 studies and intravitreal ranibizumab in 1 study) compared with those who received LPC for primary treatment of ROP.

Conclusions

Although no level I evidence was available, systematically reviewed studies with level II and III evidence showed no evidence that neurodevelopmental outcomes differed among infants who received anti-VEGF compared with LPC for primary treatment of ROP. A limitation to this assessment was that no study was powered for neurodevelopmental outcomes or to detect small differences in neurodevelopmental outcomes.

Financial disclosure(s)

Proprietary or commercial disclosure may be found in the Footnotes and Disclosures at the end of this article.

records.title: Clinical Efficacy of Switching to Faricimab in Treatment Resistant Neovascular Age-Related Macular Degeneration: Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.

content.title: Clinical Efficacy of Switching to Faricimab in Treatment Resistant Neovascular Age-Related Macular Degeneration: Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.
content.abstract:
Topic

Faricimab in the treatment of treatment-resistant neovascular age-related macular degeneration (nAMD).

Clinical relevance

While many studies on faricimab in treatment-resistant eyes have reported improvements in retinal thickness (RT), the impact on visual acuity (VA) remains inconsistent. Additionally, variability in dosing protocols-with some studies utilizing loading interval for the first 3 injections while others continuing at the prior injection interval-introduces further uncertainty regarding the optimal treatment strategy. Understanding these differences is essential for guiding clinical decision-making and maximizing patient outcomes.

Methods

This systematic review and meta-analysis followed PRISMA guidelines and was registered in PROSPERO (CRD420251000088). A systematic search of PubMed, Embase, and Scopus (February 3, 2025) identified studies evaluating the effects of switching to faricimab in treatment-resistant nAMD. Inclusion criteria required patients to have received ≥3 prior anti-VEGF injections and ≥3 faricimab injections, with reported outcomes on RT, VA, fluid status, or injection intervals. Outcomes were measured following completion of loading dose and at last follow up, ranging from 3 months to 1.5 years. Studies were assessed for bias using ROBINS-I and NIH Quality Assessment tool and assessed for certainty of evidence using GRADE. Meta-analyses were conducted using mean differences, odds ratio, and random-effects models.

Results

Fourteen studies (926 eyes) met inclusion criteria. Switching to faricimab significantly reduced RT by 46.67 µm (95% CI: 35.91-57.42, I2 = 0%, 721 eyes). Eyes that followed a loading interval were found to have greater reduction in RT than those that did not (I2 = 74.1%, 640 eyes). The odds of achieving a dry macula increased 4.35-fold (95% CI: 2.95-6.42, I2 = 64%, 379 eyes). Eyes with baseline VA <65 ETDRS letters showed a gain of 3.16 letters (95% CI: 0.80-5.52, I2 = 0%, 439 eyes). Injection intervals were extended by 1.56 weeks (95% CI: 0.71-2.40, I2 = 86%, 591 eyes). Using GRADE, 4 outcomes were graded as either very low (VA, dryness, and treatment interval) or low (RT).

Conclusion

Switching to faricimab in treatment-resistant nAMD eyes significantly improved RT with no change in VA. This effect was greater with a loading interval protocol. Overall, there was an extension of injection intervals. Further prospective studies are needed to optimize dosing strategies and assess long-term efficacy.

records.title: CILIARY NEUROTROPHIC FACTOR THERAPY FOR MACULAR TELANGIECTASIA TYPE 2: A Systematic Review.

content.title: CILIARY NEUROTROPHIC FACTOR THERAPY FOR MACULAR TELANGIECTASIA TYPE 2: A Systematic Review.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To assess the structural and functional outcomes of treatment with ciliary neurotrophic factor for patients with Type 2 macular telangiectasia (MacTel).

Methods

Studies were retrieved from inception to May 2024 from MEDLINE, Embase, and Cochrane Library databases. The primary outcome was final best-corrected visual acuity and changes in best-corrected visual acuity from baseline, while ellipsoid zone discontinuity area was a secondary outcome. Risk of bias for observational studies and randomized clinical trials were assessed using the ROBINS-1 tool and Cochrane ROB2 tools, respectively.

Results

Five studies reporting on 498 eyes of 422 patients were included in this systematic review. One randomized clinical trials of 99 eyes found decreased progression of retinal degeneration and reduced decline in reading speed in implant-treated eyes compared with sham-treated eyes. An uncontrolled Phase 1 safety trial involving 14 eyes in 7 patients with MacTel undergoing ciliary neurotrophic factor therapy demonstrated good tolerance, with no significant differences in visual acuity or retinal sensitivity between treated and untreated eyes over 36 months, although five participants experienced persistent miosis in the implanted eye. One study highlighted smaller changes in ellipsoid zone defect areas in ciliary neurotrophic factor-treated eyes compared with sham-treated eyes. Recently published data demonstrated significant structural progression slowing, although functional outcomes were variable and safety was comparable with sham aside from increased delayed dark adaptation and miosis.

Conclusion

Ciliary neurotrophic factor therapy seems to slow retinal degeneration and preserve visual function in patients with MacTel. While ciliary neurotrophic factor shows promise for earlier stages of MacTel, further trials are required to fully assess its long-term efficacy.

records.title: Comparison of Renal Adverse Events Between Intravitreal Anti-Vascular Endothelial Growth Factor Agents: A Meta-Analysis.

content.title: Comparison of Renal Adverse Events Between Intravitreal Anti-Vascular Endothelial Growth Factor Agents: A Meta-Analysis.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To compare the risk of renal adverse events, particularly acute kidney injury (AKI), between intravitreal anti-vascular endothelial growth factor (anti-VEGF) agents.

Design

Meta-analysis.

Methods

A systematic literature search was conducted on Ovid Medline, Embase, and the Cochrane Library for randomized controlled trials (RCTs) published from January 2005 to February 2024 involving adult patients receiving anti-VEGF intravitreal injections for age-related macular degeneration, diabetic macular edema, and macular edema secondary to retinal vein occlusion. The primary outcome was the comparative risk of AKI between anti-VEGF agents and sham injections. Secondary outcomes involved other renal adverse events. Subgroup analyses were conducted by specific disease indications. A random-effects model was used for meta-analysis to estimate risk ratios (RRs) and their 95% confidence intervals, with a P value of <.05 representing statistical significance. Risk of bias was assessed using the Cochrane Risk of Bias 2 (ROB2) tool, and the certainty of evidence was evaluated through the Cochrane Grading of Recommendations, Assessment, Development and Evaluation (GRADE) framework.

Results

A total of 10,031 eyes from 11 RCTs were included. No significant differences were found in the risk of acute or chronic renal conditions, obstructive uropathies, neoplasia, or infectious processes between anti-VEGF agents and sham therapy. AKI was reported in 5.4% (n = 10/185) of patients treated with bevacizumab, 1.3% (n = 6/456) with sham, 1.0% (n = 48/4724) with aflibercept, 0.8% (n = 15/1929) with faricimab, 0.5% (n = 5/1098) with brolucizumab, and 0.3% (n = 5/1639) with ranibizumab. No significant differences in AKI risk were observed between any of the anti-VEGF agents and sham (P > .05 for all comparisons). However, there was an increased risk of patient-reported symptoms with 1.25 mg bevacizumab compared to 2 mg aflibercept (RR = 3.26, 95% CI = 1.07-9.93, P = .04), driven primarily by reports of hematuria: 4.3% (bevacizumab), 0.7% (sham), 0.2% (aflibercept), 0.1% (faricimab), and 0.1% (ranibizumab).

Conclusions

US Food and Drug Administration (FDA)-approved intravitreal anti-VEGF agents do not significantly increase the risk of AKI compared to sham injections. Nevertheless, variations in patient-reported renal symptoms were observed across different anti-VEGF drugs. These variations were influenced primarily by differences in hematuria events, which may be a result of differential systemic absorption by these agents. These results underscore the importance of continuous monitoring and pharmacovigilance.

records.title: Pooled Data Meta-Analysis of Pneumatic Vitreolysis for Treatment of Vitreomacular Traction Syndrome With, And Without Full Thickness Macular Holes.

content.title: Pooled Data Meta-Analysis of Pneumatic Vitreolysis for Treatment of Vitreomacular Traction Syndrome With, And Without Full Thickness Macular Holes.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To conduct a pooled data meta-analysis assessing the efficacy and complication rates of pneumatic vitreolysis as a first-line treatment for vitreomacular traction with and without full-thickness macular holes (FTMH).

Methods

The National Library of Medicine PubMed interface, EMBASE, Scopus, and Cochrane Library were queried for articles published from May 1995 to March 2025 detailing the use of a gas injection for treatment of vitreomacular traction with or without FTMH. Efficacy and complication data were pooled and analyzed.

Results

A total of 33 studies reporting on 637 eyes with VMT treated with PVL were included. Of these, 476 eyes had VMT alone and 161 had concurrent FTMH. VMT release occurred in 76% of all eyes with rates of 49%, 67%, 71%, and 83%, for filtered air, SF6, C2F6 and C3F8 respectively. Across eyes with VMT alone, the release rate was 71%, while eyes with VMT and macular holes (MH) it was 94%, and successful MH closure rate was 40%. VMT release was higher in phakic (84%) compared to pseudophakic eyes (76%). Adverse events included development of new FTMHs in 5% of VMT-only eyes, and across all studies, retinal tears and detachments developed in 8 (1%) and 13 (2%) eyes, respectively.

Conclusion

Pneumatic vitreolysis appears to be a cost-effective treatment option for patients with vitreomacular traction without FTMH with modest to good success rates. Eyes with concurrent macular hole have a modest closure rate only. The risk of complications, including FTMH, retinal tear or detachment, must be considered.

records.title: Use of intracameral antibiotics prophylaxis in patients with posterior capsular rupture during cataract surgery: systematic review and meta-analysis.
records.publisher: Journal of cataract and refractive surgery

content.title: Use of intracameral antibiotics prophylaxis in patients with posterior capsular rupture during cataract surgery: systematic review and meta-analysis.
content.abstract:
Topic

Posterior capsular rupture (PCR) during cataract surgery predisposes patients to postoperative endophthalmitis (POE). However, little is known about the prophylactic use of intracameral antibiotics (ICA) to prevent POE after PCR. This systematic review and meta-analysis assesed the efficacy of ICA in preventing POE in patients with PCR.

Clinical relevance

PCR increases the risk of POE by more than 6-fold, emphasizing the need for targeted prophylactic strategies. This study focused on the clinical importance of ICA in reducing the incidence of POE in this high-risk population.

Methods

PubMed, Embase, and Cochrane were searched for articles published up to May 21, 2024, with the following strategy: (cataract OR phaco OR "Cataract Extraction" OR "manual small incision cataract surgery" OR phacoemulsification OR "extracapsular cataract extraction" OR ECCE) AND (intracameral OR "Intracameral Injection" OR "irrigating infusion fluid" OR "anterior chamber injection") AND (antibiotic OR moxifloxacin OR cefuroxime OR vancomycin OR cephalosporin OR prophylaxis). Studies were included that reported the incidence of endophthalmitis in patients with PCR during cataract surgery and a comparison of prophylactic ICA with no ICA. Statistical analysis was conducted using R software v. 4.3.2. The protocol was registered in PROSPERO (CRD42024558144).

Results

The initial search yielded 1660 results. After removing duplicate records and ineligible studies, 193 remained and were thoroughly reviewed based on the inclusion criteria. 9 studies consisting of 2 randomized controlled trials and 7 observational studies were included in the meta-analysis. There were a total of 153 690 patients, with 50 207 (33.6%) patients in the ICA group and 103 483 (67.3%) in the no ICA group. There was a significantly lower incidence of endophthalmitis in the ICA group (odds ratio [OR] 0.41; 95% CI 0.26-0.65; P < .001; I2 = 9%). Independently, the use of prophylactic intracameral moxifloxacin was also related to a lower risk of endophthalmitis (OR 0.33; 95% CI 0.19-0.57; P < .001; I2 = 33%).

Conclusions

The findings suggest that the use of ICA is efficient in preventing postoperative endophthalmitis in patients who had PCR during cataract surgery.

records.title: Optical Coherence Tomography Predictive Biomarkers for Visual Outcomes after Macula-Off Rhegmatogenous Retinal Detachment: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.

content.title: Optical Coherence Tomography Predictive Biomarkers for Visual Outcomes after Macula-Off Rhegmatogenous Retinal Detachment: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
content.abstract:
Topic

Systematic review and meta-analysis of preoperative optical coherence tomography (OCT) features as predictors of visual outcomes following macula-off rhegmatogenous retinal detachment (RRD) surgery.

Clinical relevance

To assess the impact of preoperatively assessed OCT parameters including photoreceptor ellipsoid zone (EZ) integrity, external limiting membrane (ELM) preservation, outer retinal corrugations (ORCs), subretinal fluid (SRF) height, intraretinal cysts (IRC), and epiretinal membrane (ERM) on post-operative best-corrected visual acuity (BCVA).

Methods

We systematically searched PubMed, Embase, and Cochrane Library databases through March 2025. Eligible studies evaluated preoperative OCT parameters as predictors of postoperative visual outcomes. Meta-analysis was performed using random-effects models with DerSimonian-Laird method to calculate pooled odds ratios (ORs) and standardized mean differences (SMDs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Risk of bias for individual studies was assessed using a Modified Newcastle-Ottawa Quality Assessment Scale. The certainty of the body of evidence for each outcome was evaluated using the GRADE (Grading of Recommendations, Assessment, Development, and Evaluation) approach.

Results

Twenty studies with 1841 eyes were included. Lower SRF height was associated with better outcomes (SMD: -0.72, 95% CI: -1.08 to -0.36; I² = 71%). Intact EZ was significantly associated with better visual outcomes (pooled OR: 3.76, 95% CI: 2.61-5.42; I² = 54%). Preserved ELM integrity was associated with better outcomes (pooled OR: 3.24, 95% CI: 2.13-4.92; I² = 49%). Absence of ORCs was associated with better outcomes (pooled OR: 2.83, 95% CI: 1.94-4.13; I² = 47%). Absence of IRC and ERM improved outcomes (OR: 2.26 and 2.64 respectively). SRF height predictive value was stronger for detachments ≤7 days. Morphologic staging systems showed strong correlation with visual outcomes (pooled r = 0.64, 95% CI: 0.52-0.74).

Conclusions

Based on low to very low-quality evidence according to GRADE assessment, preoperative OCT biomarkers may predict visual outcomes after macula-off RRD surgery, with photoreceptor layer integrity showing the strongest associations. However, the high heterogeneity, predominance of retrospective studies, and methodological limitations require that these findings be interpreted with significant caution and validated in high-quality prospective studies before clinical implementation.

records.title: Effect of Preoperative Topical 0.1% Nepafenac in Patients Undergoing Phacoemulsification With Pseudoexfoliation Syndrome or Mature Cataract.
records.publisher: Journal of cataract and refractive surgery

content.title: Effect of Preoperative Topical 0.1% Nepafenac in Patients Undergoing Phacoemulsification With Pseudoexfoliation Syndrome or Mature Cataract.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To evaluate the effect of preoperative topical 0.1% nepafenac on intraoperative pain, pupil dynamics, and surgical outcomes in eyes with pseudoexfoliation syndrome (PEX) or mature cataract undergoing phacoemulsification.

Setting

Department of Ophthalmology, Çanakkale Onsekiz Mart University Hospital, Çanakkale, Türkiye.

Design

Prospective, non-randomized comparative clinical study.

Methods

Patients with PEX or mature cataract undergoing phacoemulsification received preoperative topical 0.1% nepafenac or no nepafenac. Pupil diameters were measured from surgical videos at surgery start (T1), after intracameral epinephrine (T2), after nucleus removal (T3), after cortex aspiration (T4), and after intraocular lens implantation (T5). Intraoperative pain, complications, and surgical outcomes were assessed.

Results

A total of 126 eyes were included: 32 PEX without nepafenac, 33 PEX with nepafenac, 31 mature cataract without nepafenac, and 30 mature cataract with nepafenac. Baseline characteristics were comparable among the groups (all P > .05). In PEX eyes, nepafenac did not significantly affect pupil diameter at any time point. In mature cataract eyes, pupil diameters were similar through T3 but significantly larger with nepafenac at T4 (7.30 ± 1.05 vs 6.38 ± 1.29 mm; P = .004) and T5 (6.85 ± 1.14 vs 5.87 ± 1.29 mm; P = .003). Pain scores, complication rates, and surgical outcomes were comparable between groups.

Conclusions

Preoperative nepafenac improved maintenance of mydriasis during later surgical stages in mature cataract eyes but showed no significant benefit in PEX eyes. No significant effect on intraoperative pain or surgical outcomes was observed.

records.title: Influence of capsular tension ring implantation on dynamic in vivo capsular apposition and intraocular lens behavior in highly myopic eyes.
records.publisher: Journal of cataract and refractive surgery

content.title: Influence of capsular tension ring implantation on dynamic in vivo capsular apposition and intraocular lens behavior in highly myopic eyes.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To evaluate the dynamic in vivo capsular apposition to the intraocular lens (IOL) in highly myopic eyes after capsular tension ring (CTR) implantation using swept-source optical coherence tomography (SS-OCT), and to investigate its correlation with in-the-bag IOL behavior.

Setting

Eye Hospital of Wenzhou Medical University, Hangzhou, Zhejiang Province, China.

Design

Prospective randomized clinical trial.

Methods

Highly myopic patients undergoing cataract surgery were randomized to receive CTR implantation or not. SS-OCT was performed at 1 day, 1 week, 1 month, 3 months, and 6 months to assess capsular apposition. Postoperative aqueous depth (PAD), IOL rotation, and anterior and posterior capsular opacification (ACO/PCO) were evaluated at each follow-up visit.

Results

A total of 29 eyes with CTR implantation and 30 eyes without CTR were included. The CTR group exhibited accelerated anterior capsular apposition, demonstrated by a smaller lens-anterior capsule distance (LCD) at 1 day and a higher proportion of anterior capsular apposition at 1 week. From 1 month onward, posterior capsular apposition occurred more frequently in the CTR group. At 1 day, the average LCD positively correlated with both PAD and IOL rotation. During subsequent follow-up period, the mean capsular bend index exhibited negative correlations with the absolute changes in PAD and IOL rotational speed. The CTR group developed less severe ACO, eyes with incomplete posterior capsular apposition had a higher risk of PCO.

Conclusions

CTR implantation facilitates accelerated anterior and more complete posterior capsular apposition to the IOL in highly myopic eyes, which may contribute to improved postoperative IOL stability and a reduced incidence of capsular opacification.

records.title: Optimal target offset under asymmetric refractive loss and discrete intraocular lens power steps.
records.publisher: Journal of cataract and refractive surgery

content.title: Optimal target offset under asymmetric refractive loss and discrete intraocular lens power steps.
content.abstract: Slight myopia is often chosen during intraocular lens power selection to avoid a hyperopic result, but the appropriate offset depends on prediction uncertainty and the consequences of residual refraction. This analysis derived the target that minimizes expected loss under unequal penalties for myopic and hyperopic outcomes and assessed discrete lens choices. Under Gaussian prediction error and piecewise-linear loss, a -0.25 D target at a prediction standard deviation of 0.40 D implied a hyperopic-to-myopic loss-weight ratio of 2.8. A sensitivity analysis motivated by distance-acuity asymmetry assigned greater penalties to myopia, yielding hypothetical hyperopic targets of +0.17 to +0.39 D. With hyperopic outcomes weighted twice as heavily and refractive steps no larger than prediction standard deviation, choosing the available refraction nearest the continuous optimum added little expected loss. The analysis explains the tradeoffs implicit in habitual targeting; clinical application requires calibrated prediction errors and patient-appropriate loss functions.

records.title: Do hyperopic eyes have narrower iridocorneal angles than myopic eyes at the same anterior chamber depth? A matched study.
records.publisher: Journal of cataract and refractive surgery

content.title: Do hyperopic eyes have narrower iridocorneal angles than myopic eyes at the same anterior chamber depth? A matched study.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To compare iridocorneal angle (ICA) and other anterior segment anatomical parameters between hyperopic and myopic eyes with the same anterior chamber depth (ACD), which could have important implications for hyperopic posterior chamber phakic intraocular lens (PC-pIOL) implantation.

Setting

Private eye hospital.

Design

Retrospective observational study.

Methods

ACD, ICA, anterior chamber volume (ACV), white-to-white (WTW), and spherical equivalent were obtained from records of patients aged 21-55 and analysed using paired and regression approaches. Hyperopic and myopic eyes were matched 1:1 by ACD and compared with paired t-tests. Analysis of covariance was performed with ICA as the dependent variable, refractive group as the fixed factor and ACD as a covariate. An ICA ≥ 35 degrees was defined as a sufficiently wide angle.

Results

Forty-four hyperopic and 72 myopic eyes were included. In the paired analysis, ICA and ACV did not differ significantly between groups (p = 0.356 and 0.446 respectively). In the regression analysis, refractive group was not a significant predictor of ICA after adjustment for ACD (p = 0.193). The proportion of eyes with wide ICA increased with ACD but did not differ between groups.

Conclusion

We found no statistically significant anatomical difference in Scheimpflug-measured ICA and ACV between hyperopic and myopic eyes with the same ACD in this population. Nevertheless, the current thicker hyperopic lens design without a central hole remains an important reason for exercising greater caution with hyperopic PC-pIOL implantation.

records.title: Clinical outcomes according to the functional classification of intraocular lenses based on depth-of-field after myopic Laser in situ Keratomileusis.
records.publisher: Journal of cataract and refractive surgery

content.title: Clinical outcomes according to the functional classification of intraocular lenses based on depth-of-field after myopic Laser in situ Keratomileusis.
content.abstract:
Purpose
