content.title: Artificial intelligence in surgical decision-making across the perioperative continuum: a scoping review.
content.abstract:
Background

The role of artificial intelligence (AI) in supporting clinical decision-making across the perioperative continuum remains incompletely defined. Although the presence of many AI models that perform well in terms of their predictive performance has been established, their role in the actual surgical decision-making process in the real-world in terms of specialties and perioperative phases has not been fully mapped.

Objective

To map the existing literature on the application of AI in surgical decision-making across the perioperative continuum, describe its use in preoperative, intraoperative, and postoperative phases, and identify key barriers and gaps affecting clinical implementation.

Methods

A scoping review was conducted in accordance with the PRISMA-ScR guidelines. PubMed, Scopus, and Google Scholar were searched for studies evaluating AI applications in surgical decision-making. Eligible studies included primary research and evidence syntheses applying machine learning, deep learning, radiomics, or computer vision to diagnosis, risk stratification, surgical planning, intraoperative guidance, or postoperative outcome prediction. Study characteristics, perioperative phase, clinical application, AI methodology, and reported implementation barriers were extracted and charted using a standardized data form.

Results

Fifty- five sources of evidence were included. Sources addressing multiple or cross-phase perioperative applications constituted the largest category, while among phase-specific applications, preoperative applications were the most frequent and primarily focused on diagnosis, risk stratification, and surgical planning. Intraoperative applications were less common and were limited by data availability, workflow integration, and real-time implementation challenges. Postoperative applications mainly addressed complication prediction, survival estimation, and recovery monitoring.

Conclusion

AI in surgical decision-making is expanding rapidly, with preoperative applications showing comparatively greater evidence maturity than intraoperative and postoperative applications. However, prospective validation and real-world implementation remain limited across the perioperative continuum.

records.title: Getting your publication right - Part 4 structuring a research manuscript: A guide to understanding, detecting, and preventing plagiarism.
records.publisher: Journal of conservative dentistry and endodontics

content.title: Getting your publication right - Part 4 structuring a research manuscript: A guide to understanding, detecting, and preventing plagiarism.
content.abstract: Plagiarism is one of the most persistent ethical problems in academic and scientific publishing. Once limited to copying sentences from books, it has grown into a far more complicated challenge, driven by the internet, intense research competition, and the rapid spread of generative artificial intelligence (AI) tools. This article provides a thorough overview of plagiarism - definition, historical roots, types, contributing factors, detection tools, and regulatory frameworks with particular focus on recent developments through 2025/2026. The article pays special attention to India's regulatory approach under the University Grants Commission 2018 Regulations, the global role of the Committee on Publication Ethics, and the newly published Generative AI Transparency 2024 guidelines. The central argument is that addressing plagiarism today demands a combination of good ethical education, clear institutional policies, honest AI disclosure, and a genuine commitment to original thinking.

records.title: Biomarkers and clinical factors associated with sepsis-induced coagulopathy: A systematic review and meta-analysis.

content.title: Biomarkers and clinical factors associated with sepsis-induced coagulopathy: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
content.abstract: ObjectiveSepsis-induced coagulopathy (SIC) is a life-threatening complication that significantly impacts patient prognosis. This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to evaluate clinical and biological indicators associated with the development of SIC to facilitate early risk identification.MethodsWe searched nine databases for studies reporting predictive factors for SIC. Data were pooled using random-effects or fixed-effects models as appropriate. Methodological quality was assessed using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale.ResultsA total of 34 studies involving 37,459 patients were included. Meta-analysis revealed that several markers showed a significant association with SIC. Glycocalyx degradation emerged as a strong predictor (OR = 11.85, 95% CI: 8.59-16.34). Other associated markers included reduced Fibrinogen (OR = 4.35, 95% CI: 2.47-7.69), Albumin (OR = 2.5, 95% CI: 1.82-3.45), Neutrophil Extracellular Traps (OR = 2.4, 95% CI: 1.81-3.19), increased circulating Microparticles (OR = 1.61, 95% CI: 1.33-1.95), elevated Lactate(OR = 1.18, 95% CI: 1.13-1.23) and Thrombomodulin (OR = 1.10, 95% CI: 0.97-1.26), Procalcitonin, APACHE II score and C-reactive protein were also demonstrated predictive value for SIC occurrence.ConclusionOur findings identify multiple biological and clinical predictors associated with SIC. However, these results should be interpreted as statistical associations rather than direct causal links. These markers may assist clinicians in early recognition of high-risk patients, though further prospective trials are needed to confirm their clinical utility.RegistrationThis study was registered on the PROSPERO (CRD420250653820).

records.title: The effectiveness of virtual reality-assisted relaxation therapy in improving psychological symptoms and fatigue of breast cancer survivors: a systematic review and meta-analysis.

content.title: The effectiveness of virtual reality-assisted relaxation therapy in improving psychological symptoms and fatigue of breast cancer survivors: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
content.abstract:
Objective

This meta-analysis investigated the effect of virtual reality-assisted relaxation therapy (VR-ART) on the reduction of psychological symptoms and fatigue in breast cancer survivors.

Methods

This review followed PRISMA 2020 reporting guidelines. We searched 9 bibliographic databases, plus ClinicalTrials.gov, WHO ICTRP, and GreyGuide, for records published from database inception through September 2026, limited to Chinese- and English-language publications. Backward and forward citation chasing of included studies and related reviews was completed via Web of Science to identify additional eligible records. Parallel-group RCTs evaluating VR-assisted relaxation therapy on psychological symptoms (anxiety, depression, psychological distress) and cancer-related fatigue among breast cancer survivors were included. Two reviewers independently assessed trial risk of bias using the Cochrane RoB 2 tool.

Results

Ten RCTs with 995 breast cancer survivors were included. Pooled estimates showed VR-ART yielded statistically significant reductions in anxiety (SMD = -1.94, 95% CI [-2.49, -1.40]; P < 0.001), depressive symptoms (SMD = -1.11, 95% CI [-1.36, -0.87]; P < 0.001), and psychological distress (MD = -1.33, 95% CI [-1.99, -0.67]; P = 0.005) versus controls. effect sizes varied across treatment stages; heterogeneity for anxiety and psychological distress disappeared among trials in active treatment stages; heterogeneity for anxiety and psychological distress disappeared among trials in active treatment stages (anxiety: P = 0.91, I² = 0%; psychological distress: P = 0.79, I² = 0%). Combining sensitivity analysis and existing research, we hypothesized that the combination of chemotherapy regimen and VR interactivity might be associated with variability in effect sizes for psychological distress (P = 0.96, I² = 0%); this observation was exploratory and hypothesis-generating only. Fatigue was synthesized qualitatively rather than pooled quantitatively due to high heterogeneity, with studies reporting reduced self-reported fatigue.

Conclusion

VR-ART was associated with statistically significant reductions in anxiety, depression, psychological distress, and cancer-related fatigue among breast cancer survivors. Based on findings from exploratory subgroup analyses, we speculated that intervention timing, VR interactivity, and concurrent chemotherapy status might influence the magnitude of intervention effects. Formal testing remains absent, and further research is required to develop individualized intervention strategies and optimize treatment responses.

Systematic review registration

https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/, identifier CRD420251114925.

records.title: Clinician-Centric Explainable Artificial Intelligence Framework for Medical Imaging Diagnostics: A Systematic Review.

content.title: Clinician-Centric Explainable Artificial Intelligence Framework for Medical Imaging Diagnostics: A Systematic Review.
content.abstract: Medical imaging has evolved from conventional x-rays to advanced digital modalities, with artificial intelligence (AI), particularly deep learning, showing an increasingly central role in diagnostic support. This study presents a systematic literature review (SLR) of AI-driven medical imaging research focusing on classification-based models and explainability approaches in pneumonia detection. Using predefined inclusion criteria and PRISMA-guided screening, 95 studies were synthesized to identify dominant architectures, dataset trends, performance patterns, and persistent challenges. The analysis shows that convolutional neural networks (CNNs) and their variants remain the most frequently adopted models, accounting for the largest proportion of applications across x-ray, computed tomography scan (CT scan), and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI). Reported diagnostic performance across reviewed studies commonly exceeded 90% in accuracy and AUC, with models such as DeepMediX, XNet, Wavelet-CNN, and RadCLIP demonstrating strong predictive capability in their respective experimental settings. However, the review identifies significant gaps in explainability, clinical workflow integration, ethical compliance, and trust evaluation. Thus, this paper proposes a clinician-centric explainable artificial intelligence (CC-XAI) framework derived from literature synthesis. The framework integrates multilevel explainability, contextual clinical alignment, and human-in-the-loop feedback mechanisms to bridge the gap between black-box AI systems and real-world clinical practice. Rather than introducing a new predictive model, the framework provides a structured design blueprint for embedding explainability into medical imaging diagnostics. The findings highlight the continued dominance of deep learning in medical imaging while emphasizing the urgent need for clinician-oriented XAI frameworks to support transparency, trust, and responsible AI deployment in healthcare.

records.title: Coronary artery calcium score-emerging role for opportunistic screening on thoracic CT and novel applications.

content.title: Coronary artery calcium score-emerging role for opportunistic screening on thoracic CT and novel applications.
content.abstract: Coronary artery calcium (CAC) can be identified on thoracic CT performed for a variety of clinical indications, including routine thoracic CT, lung cancer screening CT, and attenuation correction CT. Identification of CAC on thoracic CT as part of opportunistic screening can improve the assessment of cardiovascular risk and can identify patients who may benefit from preventative medical therapies. This approach enhances early detection of coronary artery disease within existing healthcare workflows. However, at present, there are no randomized trials that assess the clinical impact of this approach. Recently, the development of artificial intelligence/machine learning (AI/ML) models has facilitated the automated identification and quantification of CAC, offering rapid and reproducible assessments. Artificial intelligence/machine learning models could reduce radiologist workload and provide end-to-end integration into routine clinical practice. Novel technologies such as photon-counting CT offer further potential for CAC detection and risk stratification through the use of high-resolution imaging and spectral imaging with virtual non-contrast images. This review discusses the evidence for opportunistic screening for CAC on thoracic CT and highlights novel applications including AI/ML assessments, CAC as a multi-system biomarker, and the potential for photon counting CT.

records.title: The impact of music intervention during emergency suturing on patients' pain and anxiety: a meta-analysis.

content.title: The impact of music intervention during emergency suturing on patients' pain and anxiety: a meta-analysis.
content.abstract:
Objective

To evaluate the effects of music intervention on pain and anxiety in patients undergoing emergency suturing.

Methods

PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library were systematically searched up to September 9, 2025. Randomized controlled trials comparing music intervention with standard care during emergency laceration repair were included. Standardized mean differences (SMDs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were pooled using a random-effects model. Heterogeneity was assessed using the I2 statistic, and evidence certainty was evaluated with the GRADE approach.

Results

Four RCTs involving 388 patients were included. Music intervention significantly reduced pain compared with standard care (SMD = -0.28, 95% CI - 0.48 to -0.08; I2 = 0%). Anxiety scores showed a borderline reduction in the music group (SMD = -0.40, 95% CI - 0.80 to 0.00; I2 = 20%). Sensitivity analyses supported the robustness of the results. The certainty of evidence was rated as low to moderate.

Conclusion

Music intervention during emergency suturing significantly reduces pain and may provide modest benefits in alleviating anxiety.

records.title: GenAI-Supported Virtual Patients in Health Care Education: Systematic Review.

content.title: GenAI-Supported Virtual Patients in Health Care Education: Systematic Review.
content.abstract:
Background

Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) is enhancing virtual patient simulations in health care education by enabling dynamic, adaptive interactions, reshaping how clinical skills are taught. A synthesis of the current evidence is needed to guide implementation and future research, given the pace of technological advancement.

Objective

This systematic review aims to synthesize empirical research on the design, implementation, and educational impact of GenAI-supported virtual patients in health care education.

Methods

A systematic search was conducted across 5 databases (CINAHL, Medline, Embase, Scopus, and Web of Science) from their inception to March 19, 2026. Reference lists of included studies and relevant systematic reviews were also screened. Peer-reviewed studies in English that evaluated GenAI-supported virtual patients using quantitative or mixed methods were included. Two reviewers independently screened studies and extracted data. Study quality and risk of bias were assessed critically using JBI (Joanna Briggs Institute) checklists, with disagreements resolved by consensus.

Results

A total of 15 studies met the inclusion criteria (total participants N=645), spanning health care disciplines, including nursing, medicine, pharmacy, radiography, and medical first-responder training. The virtual patients varied in design; input modalities included text (9 studies), voice (5 studies), or hybrid (1 study); output was text (9 studies), speech (5 studies), or both (1 study); 6 studies used 3D-embodied avatars, while 9 used nonembodied interfaces. A total of 13 studies used OpenAI GPT models (eg, ChatGPT), 1 used a fine-tuned model from a different provider, and 1 evaluated multiple model families (Claude, GPT, and open-source). Further, 6 studies used controlled experimental designs, including 3 randomized controlled trials (RCTs); the remainder were cross-sectional or prepost evaluations. Primary outcomes included user perceptions (14 studies), communication skills (4 studies), clinical reasoning (3 studies), and performance (7 studies). In controlled comparisons, GenAI-supported virtual patients consistently improved outcomes relative to control conditions: for example, enhanced clinical decision-making (RCT, n=21), ophthalmology history-taking skills (RCT, n=26), and medical history-taking performance (crossover RCT, n=20). The evidence base is characterized by brief intervention durations, a predominant reliance on single-session interactions, and a general lack of underpinning educational theory. No meta-analysis was performed due to the limited number of studies and significant heterogeneity in designs, interventions, and outcome measures.

Conclusions

The evidence supports the feasibility and acceptability of GenAI-supported virtual patients, with positive learner perceptions and promising outcomes for skills development. However, critical limitations remain in emotional-behavioral complexity, simulation adaptability, and research design rigor (eg, limited use of control groups and validated instruments). The review offers educators, instructional designers, and policymakers actionable insights for integrating dynamic, artificial intelligence-driven simulations while identifying crucial gaps-such as the need for theoretical grounding, longitudinal studies, and standardized design protocols-that must be addressed for safe and effective implementation.

records.title: Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare Administration and Clinical Informatics: A Critical Review and Governance Roadmap.

content.title: Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare Administration and Clinical Informatics: A Critical Review and Governance Roadmap.
content.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly influencing healthcare administration and clinical informatics by supporting disease diagnosis, clinical decision-making, treatment personalization, drug discovery, remote monitoring, public health surveillance, and hospital operations. However, the successful adoption of AI in healthcare depends not only on algorithmic performance, but also on its safe integration into clinical information systems, organizational workflows, and governance structures. This article presents a narrative critical review of recent advances in AI-driven healthcare, with a focus on four major domains: AI-enabled disease diagnosis, treatment personalization and clinical decision support, drug discovery and biomedical knowledge generation, and healthcare administration. Evidence from radiology, pathology, ophthalmology, dermatology, and cardiology shows that AI systems can achieve strong diagnostic performance in selected settings, while applications in electronic health records, natural language processing, telemedicine, and predictive analytics are increasingly used to support healthcare delivery and operational decision-making. At the same time, important barriers continue to limit real-world implementation, including fragmented data infrastructures, limited interoperability, poor data quality, algorithmic bias, lack of explainability, privacy and cybersecurity risks, unclear accountability, and insufficient external validation. This review critically examines these challenges and proposes a governance-oriented roadmap for responsible AI integration in healthcare administration and clinical informatics. The proposed roadmap emphasizes data readiness, model validation, workflow integration, institutional accountability, post-deployment monitoring, and workforce readiness. The findings suggest that AI can contribute to more efficient, accessible, and patient-centered healthcare only when it is implemented within trustworthy medical informatics ecosystems supported by ethical governance, human oversight, and continuous evaluation.

records.title: Large Language Models in Spine Surgery : A Narrative Review of Performance Paradox and Clinical Integration Challenges.

content.title: Large Language Models in Spine Surgery : A Narrative Review of Performance Paradox and Clinical Integration Challenges.
content.abstract: To provide a narrative synthesis of the performance paradox in large language model (LLM) applications for spine surgery, examining the disparity between technical metrics and clinical utility. A narrative review was conducted examining literature from January 2023 to February 2026 across PubMed, EMBASE, and Google Scholar. Studies evaluating LLM applications in spine surgery were included, with emphasis on newer models (GPT-4o, GPT-5, Claude, Gemini variants, DeepSeek). Studies were thematically analyzed across clinical documentation, patient communication, and surgical decision-making domains. Analysis of 42 studies revealed a consistent pattern across applications. LLMs performed strongly in structured documentation tasks, including current procedural terminology coding (area under the receiver operating characteristic curve, 0.87) and surgical classification (91% accuracy), and improved readability in patientfacing materials. Patient communication achieved high satisfaction rates but demonstrated limited emotional intelligence. In contrast, decision-making performance was more variable: in small vignette-based comparisons, LLMs showed lower raw accuracy than attending spine surgeons in complex scenarios, and guideline concordance ranged from 33% to 88% across models. Emerging evidence with nextgeneration models suggests incremental gains, but procedure-level agreement remains limited (κ=0.415 and 0.587 in minimally invasive spine surgery triage). Image-based tasks, such as Cobb angle measurement, remain particularly challenging, with all tested models failing to meet the ≤10° clinical threshold. LLMs show near-term utility in standardized text-based tasks, but current evidence does not support autonomous use in complex clinical decision-making or image-based spinal assessment. Staged implementation with mandatory human oversight remains necessary.

records.title: Effects of carbohydrate, caffeine and menthol mouth rinses on exercise performance and ratings of perceived exertion: a systematic review and network meta-analysis.

content.title: Effects of carbohydrate, caffeine and menthol mouth rinses on exercise performance and ratings of perceived exertion: a systematic review and network meta-analysis.
content.abstract:
Background

Mouth rinsing with carbohydrate (CHO), caffeine (CAF), or menthol (MEN) is a non-ingestive strategy that may enhance exercise performance and alter ratings of perceived exertion (RPE), but findings remain inconsistent. This systematic review and network meta-analysis (NMA) compared their relative effects.

Methods

This prospectively registered review (PROSPERO CRD420261282363) followed PRISMA-NMA. PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, the Cochrane Library, and SPORTDiscus were searched to 3 April 2026. Randomized controlled and crossover trials were eligible. RoB 2 and Confidence in Network Meta-Analysis (CINeMA) were used to assess risk of bias and certainty of evidence. Pairwise and network meta-analyses were performed in Stata 18.0, effects were expressed as standardized mean differences (SMDs), and rankings were based on the surface under the cumulative ranking curve (SUCRA).

Results

Fifty-seven studies involving 609 participants were included. The evidence base primarily comprised trained or physically active individuals, and the exercise protocols predominantly involved cycling- or running-based endurance tasks. CAF ranked first for time to exhaustion (SUCRA = 85.1%), work done during a fixed-time test (83.4%), and RPE (74.0%). MEN ranked first for time to complete a fixed amount of work (79.8%) and mean power (77.3%), whereas CHO ranked second across all five outcomes. The NMA showed no statistically significant differences among CHO, CAF, and MEN. Compared with placebo (PLA), CAF (SMD = 0.57, 95% CI: 0.13, 1.01) and CHO (SMD = 0.43, 95% CI: 0.11, 0.75) significantly prolonged time to exhaustion. CAF (SMD = 0.48, 95% CI: 0.11, 0.86) and CHO (SMD = 0.36, 95% CI: 0.12, 0.60) also significantly increased work done during a fixed-time test. CHO significantly reduced RPE (SMD = -0.14, 95% CI: -0.26, -0.02). No significant effects relative to PLA were observed for time to complete a fixed amount of work or mean power.

Conclusion

The relative advantages appeared outcome-specific. CAF showed the most favorable ranking trends for fatigue tolerance, sustained output, and RPE, whereas MEN ranked highest for completion efficiency and mean power. Because CHO, CAF, and MEN did not differ significantly, these rankings should be interpreted probabilistically rather than as evidence of clear superiority.

Systematic review registration

https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD420261282363, identifier CRD420261282363.

records.title: The longitudinal association between artificial sweetener intake and the risk of type 2 diabetes among adults aged 18 years and older: a systematic review and meta-analysis.

content.title: The longitudinal association between artificial sweetener intake and the risk of type 2 diabetes among adults aged 18 years and older: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
content.abstract:
Background

Artificial sweeteners are commonly used as sugar substitutes because they provide sweetness with little or no caloric content. However, the relationship between artificial sweetener consumption and type 2 diabetes (T2D) remains controversial. This meta-analysis was conducted to investigate the longitudinal association between artificial sweetener intake and T2D among adults.

Methods

Electronic databases in English and Chinese were searched for prospective studies published from inception to March 2025. Using a random-effects model, the pooled hazard ratios (HRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were calculated to investigate the longitudinal association between artificial sweetener intake and T2D among adults aged 18 years and older. Between-study heterogeneity was assessed using the I 2 statistic, while the robustness of the findings was examined using a leave-one-out sensitivity analysis. Publication bias was evaluated by inspection of funnel plots and Egger's regression test.

Results

A total of six cohort studies including 721,003 participants were analyzed in this meta-analysis. Compared with those with low or no consumption of artificial sweeteners, participants with higher artificial sweetener intake were more likely to develop T2D (pooled HR = 1.31, 95% CI = 1.16-1.49). Substantial heterogeneity was observed across studies (I 2 = 86.02%), while the overall estimate remained stable in sensitivity analysis. No significant publication bias was observed among the studies included in this meta-analysis.

Conclusion

A longitudinal association was observed between artificial sweetener intake and the risk of developing T2D among adults. This study has important public health implications. The findings of this study highlight that artificial sweeteners may not be a completely risk-free alternative to sugar in dietary interventions aimed at reducing high-energy sugar intake and suggest that their potential adverse metabolic effects should be considered in public health policy-making and clinical dietary recommendations regarding artificial sweetener intake.

records.title: Application of artificial intelligence large language models in drug target discovery.

content.title: Application of artificial intelligence large language models in drug target discovery.
content.abstract: Drug target discovery is a fundamental aspect of contemporary drug research and development. However, the use of conventional biochemical screening, omics analysis, and related approaches is constrained by substantial technical complexity and significant resource requirements. With the advancement of artificial intelligence-based large language models, notable progress has been achieved in drug target identification. During target mining, large language models with natural language comprehension capabilities can efficiently integrate literature data resources and systematically analyze disease-associated biological pathways and potential targets. Notably, models specifically designed for biomolecular "language" have demonstrated advantages across multiple aspects. The genomics-focused large language model has significantly enhanced the accuracy of pathogenic gene variant identification and gene expression prediction. In transcriptomics, large language models enable comprehensive reconstruction of gene regulatory networks. In proteomics, advancements have been made in protein structure analysis, function prediction, and interaction inference. Additionally, the single-cell multi-omics large language model facilitates data integration across different omics technologies. These technological advancements provide multi-dimensional biological evidence supporting drug target discovery and contribute to a more efficient screening process for candidate targets. The development of these models is generally based on deep neural networks of Transformer architecture, and powerful representation capabilities are obtained through large-scale unsupervised pre-training (such as mask language modeling, autoregressive prediction) combined with task-specific supervised fine-tuning. This review systematically examines recent advancements in the application of large language models in drug target discovery, emphasizing existing technical challenges and potential future research directions.

records.title: Artificial intelligence and robotic technologies redefining precision and personalization in orthopedic surgery: a narrative review.

content.title: Artificial intelligence and robotic technologies redefining precision and personalization in orthopedic surgery: a narrative review.
content.abstract: The integration of artificial intelligence and robotic technologies is transforming orthopedic surgery by enhancing diagnostic accuracy, surgical precision, and personalized rehabilitation. This review summarizes the development of these technologies, explains their underlying principles, and evaluates their applications across diagnosis, preoperative planning, intraoperative navigation, and postoperative recovery. Artificial intelligence improves early detection of musculoskeletal conditions, supports risk prediction, and enables patient-specific treatment planning through advanced data analysis and image interpretation. Robotic systems enhance surgical consistency and safety by providing real-time guidance, mechanical precision, and controlled execution of complex procedures. Together, these technologies reduce variability, lower complication rates, and support individualized rehabilitation through wearable sensors, motion analysis, and virtual reality platforms. Despite these advances, significant challenges persist, including limited algorithm transparency, data fragmentation, bias, financial barriers, and unresolved ethical and regulatory questions. Future progress is expected to arise from autonomous surgical systems, integration with emerging technologies such as digital twins and high-speed communication networks, and improved data sharing frameworks that support global collaboration. By outlining current capabilities, limitations, and future directions, this review provides a foundation for the responsible and effective adoption of intelligent technologies in orthopedic care.

records.title: Effects of different metabolic equivalent of task on glycaemic control in children and adolescents with type 1 diabetes mellitus: a systematic review and meta-analysis.

content.title: Effects of different metabolic equivalent of task on glycaemic control in children and adolescents with type 1 diabetes mellitus: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
content.abstract:
Objective

This systematic review and meta-analysis investigated the impact of different metabolic equivalent of task (MET) levels on glycaemic control in children and adolescents with type 1 diabetes mellitus (T1DM).

Methods

Following PRISMA 2020 guidelines, PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, SPORTDiscus, and the Cochrane Library were searched up to July 2025 for randomized controlled trials comparing exercise interventions with routine care in T1DM patients aged 5-18 years. The primary outcome was HbA1c; secondary outcomes included fasting blood glucose, daily insulin dose, and time in range. MET values were calculated as intensity (MET) × duration (minutes) × frequency (per week). Subgroup analyses examined low (<600), moderate (600-1,200), and high (>1,200 METs-min/week) MET levels. Effect sizes were pooled using random-effects models.

Results

Fourteen RCTs involving 543 participants were included. Exercise significantly reduced HbA1c (WMD = -0.83%, 95% CI: -1.34% to -0.33%, p < 0.001) and fasting blood glucose (WMD = -41.38 mg/dL, 95% CI: -61.23 to -21.53, p < 0.001). Subgroup analyses showed the largest numerical HbA1c reduction in the moderate MET group (WMD = -1.21%, 95% CI: -1.94 to -0.49, p < 0.05), followed by the low MET group (WMD = -0.50%, 95% CI: -1.35 to 0.34, p > 0.05) and the high MET group (WMD = -0.30%, 95% CI: -1.12 to 0.52, p > 0.05); however, the test for differences between subgroups was not statistically significant (Q = 3.05 p = 0.22).

Conclusion

The moderate MET group showed the largest numerical HbA1c reduction, although between-subgroup differences were not statistically significant. These findings support evidence-based exercise prescription in this population, though further research is needed to clarify dose-response relationships and long-term outcomes.

Systematic review registration

Unique Identifier, CRD42024563752.

records.title: The Effectiveness of Parent-Targeted Digital Health Interventions on Breastfeeding Practices: Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.

content.title: The Effectiveness of Parent-Targeted Digital Health Interventions on Breastfeeding Practices: Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.
content.abstract:
Background

Global breastfeeding rates remain below recommended levels. Parent-targeted digital health interventions (DHIs), including mobile health (mHealth) and eHealth strategies, offer a scalable way to support breastfeeding, but their effectiveness remains uncertain.

Objective

The aim of this study is to explore the effectiveness of parent-targeted DHIs for improving breastfeeding outcomes.

Methods

In total, 7 databases were searched on December 9, 2025, for randomized controlled trials (RCTs) involving parents of children younger than 5 years of age. Eligible interventions aimed to promote breastfeeding and were primarily delivered via digital mediums. Primary outcomes of interest included exclusive breastfeeding (EBF), any breastfeeding, and breastfeeding duration. Secondary outcomes included breastfeeding self-efficacy, cost-effectiveness, and adverse events. Random effects meta-analyses were conducted in accordance with Cochrane methods, and results were reported following PRISMA (Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses) guidelines. Risk of bias was assessed using the Cochrane Risk of Bias 2 tool, and certainty of evidence was graded using the Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development, and Evaluation approach.

Results

In total, 46 (39 RCTs and 7 cluster RCTs) studies, including 33,785 participants from 18 diverse countries, were included. A total of 25 of the interventions focused on mHealth strategies, 8 were delivered via computer-based eHealth, 4 by telehealth, and 9 were delivered by eHealth or mHealth combined with telehealth. Risk of bias was indicated with "some concerns" or "high risk" for 41 (89%) studies. Pooled results indicated that DHIs can significantly improve the odds of EBF (odds ratio 2.58, 95% CI 1.91-3.50; I2=83%; 39 trials, 11,601 participants); however, considerable heterogeneity was present, and certainty of evidence was very low. Pooled results indicated with moderate certainty that DHIs may improve breastfeeding duration (standardized mean difference 0.48, 95% CI 0.29-0.67; I2=0%; 7 trials, 716 participants). Results suggest that DHIs have no effect on the odds of any breastfeeding (odds ratio 1.09, 95% CI 0.90-1.31; I2=19%; 21 trials, 8991 participants), but the certainty of evidence is very low. Cost or cost-effectiveness and adverse events were scarcely reported.

Conclusions

This review provides a comprehensive synthesis of global evidence exploring the impacts of parent-targeted DHIs on breastfeeding outcomes, spanning diverse cultural and health system contexts. Our results suggest that parent-targeted DHIs represent a promising strategy for improving key breastfeeding indicators, such as EBF and breastfeeding duration with very low to moderate certainty, as current evidence is limited by variable risk of bias, potential publication bias, and substantial heterogeneity. DHIs could have a complementary role as part of the health care and support provided to parents during the first 2000 days. Future trials should seek to minimize possible biases as well as capture key scale-up outcomes to justify embedding such innovations within existing health systems and structures.

records.title: Artificial intelligence in prostate cancer imaging: A mini-review of current applications and future directions.

content.title: Artificial intelligence in prostate cancer imaging: A mini-review of current applications and future directions.
content.abstract: This mini-review synthesizes evidence from recent studies to provide an updated perspective on current applications, methodological challenges, and future directions for artificial intelligence (AI) in multiparametric magnetic resonance imaging (mpMRI) based prostate cancer (CaP) imaging. CaP remains the most frequently diagnosed noncutaneous malignancy among men worldwide and a leading cause of cancer-related mortality. mpMRI has become the reference imaging modality for detection, localization, and risk stratification, with the Prostate Imaging-Reporting and Data System (PI-RADS) improving standardization. However, inter-reader variability and the time-intensive nature of mpMRI interpretation persist, even among expert radiologists. AI, encompassing machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL) methods, offers the potential to enhance CaP imaging by improving accuracy, consistency, and efficiency. Applications include automated lesion detection and segmentation, PI-RADS scoring standardization, and radiomics-based risk prediction. Radiomics enables the extraction of high-dimensional quantitative features from mpMRI, which, when integrated with clinical or genomic data, can improve predictive modeling for clinically significant CaP, extracapsular extension, and lymph node metastasis. Despite rapid advancements, challenges remain in data heterogeneity, generalizability, lack of standardized feature extraction, and limited external validation. The "black-box" nature of many DL models also complicates clinical trust and regulatory approval. Future directions include the integration of explainable AI, federated learning for privacy-preserving multi-institutional training, and real-time AI assistance during targeted biopsies or active surveillance.

records.title: Dumbbell Bench Press and Dumbbell Fly Elicit Similar Pectoralis Major Muscle Hypertrophy in Recreationally Trained Men.
records.publisher: Journal of strength and conditioning research

content.title: Dumbbell Bench Press and Dumbbell Fly Elicit Similar Pectoralis Major Muscle Hypertrophy in Recreationally Trained Men.
content.abstract:
Abstract

Dell'Avanzi, FG, Enes, A, Alves-Marques, F, Costa-Rodrigues, J, Bello, G, Seima, G, Nass, G, Moreira, NF, Santana, C, Mohan, AE, Piñero, A, Schoenfeld, BJ, and Souza-Junior, TP. Dumbbell bench press and dumbbell fly elicit similar pectoralis major muscle hypertrophy in recreationally trained men. J Strength Cond Res XX(X): 000-000, 2026-Exercise selection is one of the main resistance training (RT) variables for eliciting inhomogeneous muscle growth. Whether exercises that differ in resistance moment arm elicit whole- and nonuniform hypertrophy of the pectoralis major remains unclear. This study investigated the effects of the dumbbell bench press (DBP) and dumbbell fly (DFLY) on pectoralis major muscle thickness (MT). Twenty-six young healthy men (RT experience 3.3 ± 3.1 years) were allocated to DBP or DFLY groups, training twice a week over a 10-week period. The weekly set number was individualized according to subjects' previous RT pectoralis major volume. Pectoralis major MT was assessed by ultrasound imaging at medial (30%), intermediate (50%), and lateral (70%) sites at baseline and postintervention. Our mixed-model analysis indicated a main effect for time (p < 0.05) but no time-by-group interaction for the medial site (p = 0.500), intermediate site (p = 0.864), lateral site (p = 0.720), and the sum of the MT across sites (p = 0.985). Therefore, both exercises elicited similar general and regional hypertrophy on pectoralis major MT in recreationally trained individuals. Coaches and practitioners can select DBP or DFLY when targeting pectoralis major muscle development in recreationally trained men based on personal preference and goals within the RT program.

records.title: Is plant-based protein supplementation as effective as whey protein? A systematic review and meta-analysis in untrained adults undergoing resistance training.
records.publisher: Journal of the International Society of Sports Nutrition

content.title: Is plant-based protein supplementation as effective as whey protein? A systematic review and meta-analysis in untrained adults undergoing resistance training.
content.abstract:
Background

Dietary protein supplements are commonly consumed to support increases in lean body mass among healthy adults engaged in resistance training (RT). Although whey protein has been extensively investigated, plant-based protein supplements have emerged as a viable alternative for individuals who avoid animal-derived products.

Methods

The present study aims to evaluate, through a systematic review and meta-analysis, the effects of plant-based versus whey protein supplementation on body composition in untrained adults (18-59 years) undergoing RT, using Dual-Energy X-Ray Absorptiometry (DEXA). The systematic review was conducted according to the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) 2020 checklist and was registered in PROSPERO (CRD420251145410). Searches were conducted in PubMed, Web of Science, and ScienceDirect, identifying 5 studies that met the inclusion criteria for qualitative synthesis and meta-analysis.

Results

When combined with RT, both plant-based and whey protein supplementation were associated with improvements in lean body mass (LBM) and body fat mass (BFM), with no significant between-group differences observed.

Conclusions

Thus, soy- and pea-based protein supplements may support favorable body composition changes in adults initiating RT and could be considered practical nutritional options for individuals seeking alternatives to whey protein. Regarding chia-based protein, the available evidence is currently limited to a single study that did not demonstrate significant changes in lean body mass; therefore, firm conclusions regarding its efficacy cannot be drawn at this time.

records.title: How Often Should Volume Increase? Effects of Different Volume-Progression Frequencies on Strength and Hypertrophy Adaptations in Women.
records.publisher: Journal of strength and conditioning research

content.title: How Often Should Volume Increase? Effects of Different Volume-Progression Frequencies on Strength and Hypertrophy Adaptations in Women.
content.abstract:
Abstract

Enes, A, Macedo, ACG, Nass, G, Costa-Rodrigues, J, Alves-Marques, F, Santana, C, Dell'Avanzi, FG, Rodrigues, BG, Alves, RC, De Souza, EO, and Souza-Junior, TP. How often should volume increase? Effects of different volume-progression frequencies on strength and hypertrophy adaptations in females. J Strength Cond Res XX(X): 000-000, 2026-Resistance training (RT) volume is an important programming variable for strength and hypertrophy. However, how frequently RT volume should be progressed remains unclear. Thus, we investigated the effects of progressively increasing RT volume by 2 weekly sets targeting the quadriceps femoris every 2 weeks (2 W) or every 4 weeks (4 W) over a 12-week period in recreationally trained women. Using a within-subject design and accounting for previous RT volume, 21 subjects (age 23.3 ± 3.9 years; RT experience 1.1 ± 0.7 years) had their limbs assigned to one of the 2 conditions: 2 weeks (2 W) or 4 weeks (4 W). 45° leg-press 1-repetition maximum (1RM) and the sum of muscle thickness (∑MT) of the proximal (30%), middle (50%), and distal (70%) portions of the lateral thigh were assessed at baseline and after 12 weeks. Our mixed-model analysis indicated a main effect of time for 1RM (p < 0.0001), with no difference between the 2 and 4 W conditions (p = 0.317). Similarly, regarding the ∑MT, the analysis indicated a main effect of time (p < 0.001), with no difference between the conditions (p = 0.616). Within the relatively high training volumes examined, progressing the RT volume by 2 weekly sets every 2 or 4 weeks did not elicit detectable differences in strength and hypertrophy adaptations over 12 weeks in recreationally trained women.

records.title: Lower-Body Strength and Hypertrophy Adaptations in Response to Concurrent Training in Trained Young Males.
records.publisher: Journal of strength and conditioning research

content.title: Lower-Body Strength and Hypertrophy Adaptations in Response to Concurrent Training in Trained Young Males.
content.abstract:
Abstract

Gomes, M, Costa, M, Pezarat-Correia, P, and Mendonca, GV. Lower-body strength and hypertrophy adaptations in response to concurrent training in trained young males. J Strength Cond Res XX(X): 000-000, 2026-This study examined the interference effect of concurrent training (CT) on maximal and explosive strength and muscle morphology in trained young males. Thirty subjects were randomly assigned to endurance training (E), resistance training (R), or CT for 11 weeks. The intervention comprised 2 mesocycles: weeks 1-5 emphasizing maximal strength, and weeks 6-11 targeting explosive strength. Assessments were conducted at baseline, mid-training, and post-training, and included leg-press maximal voluntary isometric contraction (MVIC), rate of force development (RFD), countermovement jump kinetics, and vastus lateralis cross-sectional area and pennation angle. Maximal voluntary isometric contraction increased only in the R group (18.4 ± 10.2%, p = 0.015). Peak RFD improved in both R (31.8 ± 23.2%) and CT (23.1 ± 27.9%), although with distinct time courses: R improved progressively across both mesocycles, whereas CT improved only during the second. Early-phase RFD (0-50 ms) increased in the R group from mid-training onward, whereas the CT group improved only from mid- to post-training (38.3 ± 40.4%, p = 0.021), accompanied by greater quadriceps electromyographic activity (p < 0.05). No changes in RFD were observed in E during training. Countermovement jump positive impulse improved in both R (12.7 ± 9.0%) and CT (8.8 ± 8.3%, p < 0.05), with no evidence of interference in jump-related explosive performance. Cross-sectional area increased in both R (17.0 ± 13.0%) and CT (8.8 ± 9.4%, p < 0.05). Pennation angle increased in CT (10.1 ± 12.9%) and R (18.6 ± 15.1%). These findings indicate that, although CT may limit MVIC development and delay early-phase RFD adaptations, it does not hinder explosive performance when resistance training is oriented toward rapid-strength development. Thus, CT can be effectively implemented in trained individuals when resistance training is periodized to emphasize neural-driven explosive or hypertrophy-related adaptations.

records.title: Effects of In-Season Contrast Strength Training on Jump Performance and Sprint Ability in Female Field Hockey Players.
records.publisher: Journal of strength and conditioning research

content.title: Effects of In-Season Contrast Strength Training on Jump Performance and Sprint Ability in Female Field Hockey Players.
content.abstract:
Abstract

Chilingirian-Padrón, R, Álvarez-Yates, T, and García-García, O. Effects of in-season contrast strength training on jump performance and sprint ability in female field hockey players. J Strength Cond Res XX(X): 000-000, 2026-The purpose of this study was to examine the effects of a 6-week in-season contrast strength training program incorporating sport-specific tasks on neuromuscular performance in sub-elite female field hockey players. Twenty-five athletes completed a pre-post single-cohort intervention integrated into their regular team schedule. Each session consisted of 3 sequential blocks: (a) a high-load strength exercise targeting maximal strength or hypertrophy (70-85% 1 repetition maximum [1RM]); (b) a biomechanically related explosive action performed at low load (∼30% 1RM) and high execution velocity; and (c) a high-speed sport-specific task. Jump performance was assessed using bilateral and unilateral countermovement jumps (CMJs) and free arm CMJ, whereas sprint ability was evaluated through 10- and 20-m sprints. A mixed-model repeated-measures analysis of variance was used to determine the effects of the intervention, with Time (Pre, Post) as within-subject factor and Playing Position (defenders, midfielders, forwards) as between-subject factor, with the level of significance set at p ≤ 0.05. Significant improvements were observed in all jump and sprint assessments: jump performance increased by 5.7-29.6%, whereas sprint ability improved by 1.6-1.9%. These findings indicate that 6 weeks of contrast strength training incorporating high-speed sports-specific tasks performed during the competitive season elicited meaningful improvements in stretch-shortening cycle-related jump performance and sprint ability in sub-elite female field hockey players.

records.title: Comparative Effects of Resistance Training and High-Intensity Interval Training on Body Composition, Metabolic Health, and Functional Strength in Overweight and Obese Adults: A 12-Week Randomized Controlled Trial.
records.publisher: Journal of strength and conditioning research

content.title: Comparative Effects of Resistance Training and High-Intensity Interval Training on Body Composition, Metabolic Health, and Functional Strength in Overweight and Obese Adults: A 12-Week Randomized Controlled Trial.
content.abstract: Petisco-Rodríguez, C, Barroso-Hernández, Á, Bartolomé-Sánchez, I, and Crego, A. Comparative effects of resistance training and high-intensity interval training on body composition, metabolic health, and functional strength in overweight and obese adults: A 12-week randomized controlled trial. J Strength Cond Res XX(X): 000-000, 2026-The aim of this study was to compare the effects of 2 training programs on anthropometric and physiological variables in overweight and obese adults. Ninety subjects (age = 39.9 ± 10.4 years; body mass index (BMI) = 31.0 ± 4.3 kg·m-2) were randomly assigned to a resistance training group (RG; n = 30), a high-intensity interval training (HIIT) group (HG; n = 30), or a nontraining control group (CG; n = 30). Both the RG and HG performed 2 weekly sessions for 12 weeks. The RG completed 8 upper-body and lower-body resistance exercises at 70% of 1 repetition maximum, while the HG performed high-intensity intervals at 80% of the maximum heart rate. A 3 (group: CG, RG, HG) × 2 (time: pre, post) mixed ANOVA revealed significant effects on the BMI, body fat, and fasting glucose. Both training groups showed similar improvements in all measures from preintervention to postintervention. Compared with CG, RG and HG had reduced body fat and BMI, while RG demonstrated greater gains in muscle mass, fasting glucose, and grip strength. Paired t-tests confirmed significant within-group improvements in BMI, body fat, grip strength, and fasting glucose in the RG and HG. Statistical significance was set at p < 0.017 after the Bonferroni correction. These findings suggest that both resistance training and HIIT enhance the body composition of overweight and obese adults. However, resistance training may provide additional benefits in muscular fitness and glycemic control, supporting its role as a practical strategy for improving metabolic health in this population.

records.title: Effectiveness of Pelvic Floor Muscle Training in Women Soccer Players and Its Relationship With Quality of Life and Pelvic Floor Muscle Strength: A Randomized Controlled Pilot Study.
records.publisher: Journal of strength and conditioning research

content.title: Effectiveness of Pelvic Floor Muscle Training in Women Soccer Players and Its Relationship With Quality of Life and Pelvic Floor Muscle Strength: A Randomized Controlled Pilot Study.
content.abstract:
Abstract

Sebastian-Rico, JM, Muñoz-Fernández, MJ, Martínez-Aranda, LM, Calvo-Lluch, Á, and Ortega-Becerra, M. Effectiveness of pelvic floor muscle training in women soccer players and its relationship with quality of life and pelvic floor muscle strength: a randomized controlled pilot study. J Strength Cond Res XX(X): 000-000, 2026-This study investigated the effects of a 6-week pelvic floor muscle training (PFMT) program on muscle strength, function, and the prevalence of related dysfunctions in professional female soccer players using a randomized controlled pilot study design. Twenty nulliparous professional soccer players from the Spanish professional league (2024-2025 season) were randomly assigned to an experimental group (n = 12) or a control group (n = 8). Assessments included anthropometric data, validated questionnaires (International Consultation on Incontinence Questionnaire-Short Form and Broome Pelvic Muscle Self-Efficacy Scale), clinical interviews, and physical examination using the PERFECT method and manometry. The intervention consisted of a 6-week supervised PFMT program (4 sessions/week, 30 minutes each) progressed through 4 phases: education, proprioception, strengthening, and functional integration. Results showed significant group × time interactions for pelvic floor self-efficacy (Broome Pelvic Muscle Self-Efficacy Scale), with scores in the PFMT group increasing by 48.8 and 59.6% (p < 0.05), representing large between-group effect sizes (d = 0.91-1.26). Pelvic floor muscle performance increased by 122.4% in the intervention group (d = 1.25), whereas no meaningful changes were observed in the control group. No adverse events were reported. In conclusion, a 6-week supervised PFMT program is an effective and safe intervention for professional female soccer players, significantly improving muscle function and self-efficacy. These findings support the integration of PFMT for both therapeutic and preventive purposes in elite, high-impact sports environments.

records.title: Performance and Physiological Responses to Strength Training Programs in Elite Judo Athletes.
records.publisher: Journal of strength and conditioning research

content.title: Performance and Physiological Responses to Strength Training Programs in Elite Judo Athletes.
content.abstract:
Abstract

Campos, BT, Rodrigues, JGdS, Cal Abad, CC, Bachi, ALL, dos Santos, CMM, Tritto, AC, Kons, RL, Penna, EM, and Prado, LS. Performance and physiological responses to strength training programs in elite judo athletes. J Strength Cond Res XX(X): 000-000, 2026-This study compared the effects of 2 short-term strength training models, block planning (BP) and undulating planning (UP), on performance, physiological, and perceptual responses in elite judo athletes. We hypothesized that BP would induce greater physiological strain due to the concentration of training stimuli. Eighteen judokas (14 men and 4 women) were randomly assigned to BP (n = 9) or UP (n = 9) for 4 weeks, performing 6 weekly strength sessions alongside technical-tactical training. Performance outcomes included countermovement jump (CMJ), muscle power (back squat and bent-over row), and the Special Judo Fitness Test (SJFT). Monitoring variables included internal load, heart rate variability (HRV), and well-being, while physiological markers included creatine kinase, tumor necrosis factor-α (TNF-α), and cortisol. Data were analyzed using 2-way repeated-measures ANOVA (p < 0.05). Both groups improved SJFT performance (p < 0.01), with no between-group differences. Block planning increased lower-limb peak power (p = 0.01; d = 0.90), whereas UP showed no meaningful change. Upper-limb power and CMJ did not change in either group. Internal load showed different temporal patterns between models. Block planning presented higher HRVcv values (p = 0.04), indicating greater autonomic perturbation. Creatine kinase and TNF-α increased over time in both groups (p ≤ 0.05), while cortisol showed an interaction without clear post hoc differences. In conclusion, BP improved lower-limb power but increased physiological strain, whereas UP elicited similar judo-specific improvements with lower recovery demands. These findings highlight the importance of training organization for balancing performance and recovery in elite judo athletes.

records.title: Do Putative Human Reticulospinal Tract Properties Adapt Following Short-Term Isometric Resistance Training?
records.publisher: Medicine and science in sports and exercise

content.title: Do Putative Human Reticulospinal Tract Properties Adapt Following Short-Term Isometric Resistance Training?
content.abstract:
Purpose

The primary purpose of this study was to investigate whether isometric resistance training (RT) leads to reticulospinal tract (RST) adaptations.

Methods

A "RT group" of 30 healthy adults completed 4 weeks (15 sessions) of volume-matched unilateral elbow flexion RT involving high (32 repetitions/session at 70% maximal voluntary torque [MVT]) or low (64 repetitions/session at 35%MVT) loads. An additional 15 participants served as controls (CON group). Pre- and post-test MVT, RST properties (RST gain ratio derived from the StartReact assessment; startling auditory stimulus-conditioned/control motor evoked potential [MEP] ratio; and startling stimulus-conditioned/control cervicomedullary MEP [CMEP] ratio), CST excitability and intracortical inhibition properties (in response to transcranial magnetic stimulation) were assessed.

Results

MVT increased more in the RT group (+12.8%; n = 30) vs. CON group (-4.3%; n = 15; group (2) × time (2), p = 0.001). However, changes in RST properties assessed using a series of indirect measures did not differ between the RT group (-1.4% to 6.6%; n = 30) and CON group (-4.5% to 10.5%; n = 15; group (2) × time (2), 0.352 ≤ p ≤ 0.834).

Conclusions

RST adaptations within a sample of healthy young men and women, assessed using various indirect measurement approaches, did not occur following only 4 weeks of isometric elbow flexion RT. These findings add to the currently limited scientific evidence from short-term human RT intervention studies available to inform the use of RT for healthy individuals or patients primarily targeting the development of RST function.

records.title: The effects of a 4-week protein overfeeding protocol on body composition and influence of FTO genotype in exercise-trained men and women.
records.publisher: Journal of the International Society of Sports Nutrition

content.title: The effects of a 4-week protein overfeeding protocol on body composition and influence of FTO genotype in exercise-trained men and women.
content.abstract:
Background

High-protein diets have consistently been associated with favorable changes in body composition in both sedentary and exercise-trained populations. Despite abundant evidence supporting protein intakes above the recommended dietary allowance (RDA) for active individuals, the effects of deliberate protein overfeeding, particularly in those already consuming adequate protein, remain incompletely characterized. The primary purpose of this study was to examine the effects of a 4-week protein overfeeding protocol on body composition in exercise-trained men and women. The secondary purpose was to determine whether body composition adaptations differed by FTO rs9939609 genotype.

Methods

Fifty-six exercise-trained men and women (age: 22.40 ± 5.78 years; body mass: 75.47 ± 14.98 kg; BMI: 24.52 ± 3.50 kg/m2; resistance training: 5.12 ± 3.35 h/week) were enrolled in a 4-week dietary intervention. Participants were instructed to increase their daily protein intake by approximately 20% above baseline while maintaining habitual training. Body composition was assessed pre- and post-intervention using a multi-frequency bioelectrical impedance device (InBody® 270). Dietary intake was self-monitored via MyFitnessPal®. Thirty-five participants completed both pre- and post-testing assessments and constituted the primary analysis. Linear regression models adjusted for baseline values indicated that FTO genotype was not a significant predictor of body composition changes (p > 0.05).

Results

Protein intake trended toward a significant increase over the 4-week period (pre: 146 ± 66 g/day vs. post: 164 ± 79 g/day; p = 0.053), representing an approximate 12% increase. Total energy intake, carbohydrate, and fat intake did not significantly change. Lean body mass increased significantly (pre: 59.95 ± 14.14 kg vs. post: 60.62 ± 14.42 kg; p = 0.005; Cohen's d = 0.31) and total body water increased significantly (pre: 43.85 ± 10.35 L vs. post: 44.34 ± 10.55 L; p = 0.005). Fat mass (p = 0.424), body fat percentage (p = 0.149), and total body mass (p = 0.09) did not significantly change.

Conclusions

A 4-week modest protein overfeeding protocol in exercise-trained men and women was associated with a significant increase in lean body mass and total body water without concomitant increases in fat mass. These adaptations were not modified by FTO rs9939609 genotype. These findings support the contention that higher protein intakes do not promote fat accretion and may facilitate improvements in body composition in trained individuals.

records.title: Beyond the Hangover: Associations Between Binge Drinking, Health, and Performance in Young Adult Resistance-Trained Females.
records.publisher: Medicine and science in sports and exercise

content.title: Beyond the Hangover: Associations Between Binge Drinking, Health, and Performance in Young Adult Resistance-Trained Females.
content.abstract:
Purpose

The present study aimed to evaluate associations between resistance training and binge drinking in relation to musculoskeletal composition, physical fitness, cognitive function, and psychological wellness in young adult females.

Methods

Participants were categorized into four groups: sedentary low alcohol consumers (SL; n=12), sedentary binge drinkers (SB; n=12), resistance-trained low alcohol consumers (RTL; n=12), and resistance-trained binge drinkers (RTB; n=12). Measurements included body composition via DEXA scan, muscle quality via ultrasonography, and insulin sensitivity via oral glucose tolerance test. Physical performance was assessed using maximum chair stand power, vertical jump, broad jump, knee extensor torque, grip strength, and push-ups to failure. Tests and questionnaires were used to assess cognitive function and psychological wellness.

Results

Resistance-trained females had lower body fat than sedentary females (RTL = 29.28±4.27%; RTB = 29.03±3.67%; SL = 37.18±5.32%; SB = 34.83±3.54%; p<0.05), and RTL had more fat-free mass than SL and SB (RTL = 48.31±5.81 kg; SL = 38.08±6.59 kg; SB = 40.37±6.05 kg; both p<0.05). There were no differences between RTL and RTB in bone mineral density, muscle quality, or physical performance. RTL outperformed SL and SB on vertical jump (both p<0.05) while RTB outperformed SL and SB on broad jump. RTL had lower fasting blood glucose than RTB (88.92±12.09 mg/dL and 103.17 ± 10.21 mg/dL, respectively; p=0.008), and lower postprandial blood glucose than all groups (RTL = 103.83±19.82 mg/dL; RTB = 137.58±21.54 mg/dL; SL = 148.50±44.60 mg/dL; SB = 139.25±14.49 mg/dL; all p<0.05).

Conclusions

The results suggest that ≥1 year of binge drinking is associated with poorer metabolic health without differences in performance in young females. Further, frequent RT may mitigate the effects of binge drinking on body composition.

records.title: Exploratory serum renal biomarker and eGFR responses to high-protein diets during resistance versus concurrent training in resistance-trained men.
records.publisher: Journal of the International Society of Sports Nutrition

content.title: Exploratory serum renal biomarker and eGFR responses to high-protein diets during resistance versus concurrent training in resistance-trained men.
content.abstract:
Background

High protein intake is common among resistance-trained athletes, but its association with renal biomarkers across different exercise modalities remains uncertain. This study investigated whether consuming a high-protein diet (3.2 g·kg⁻¹·d⁻¹) during 16 weeks of resistance training (RT) or concurrent training (CT) affects renal biomarkers and estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) in resistance-trained men.

Methods

Forty-eight resistance-trained men (26 ± 6 years; BMI 25.6 ± 2.9 kg·m⁻²) were randomized to 16 weeks of RT or CT (4 sessions·wk⁻¹) while consuming either 1.6 or 3.2 g·kg⁻¹·d⁻¹ of protein in a 2 × 2 factorial design. Forty-four participants with complete pre- and post-intervention data were analyzed. Fasting blood samples were assessed for blood urea nitrogen (BUN), BUN/creatinine ratio, cystatin C, and eGFR calculated using the CKD-EPI creatinine (2021), cystatin C (2012), and creatinine-cystatin C (2021) equations. Within-group changes were evaluated using paired t-tests, and factorial effects were assessed using linear mixed-effects models (Time × Training × Protein).

Results

No statistically significant Time × Protein or Time × Training × Protein interactions were detected for any renal biomarker or eGFR estimate (all p ≥ 0.182). No significant within-group changes occurred in the 1.6 g·kg⁻¹·d⁻¹ groups (all p > 0.05). In both 3.2 g·kg⁻¹·d⁻¹ groups, BUN and cystatin C increased (all p ≤ 0.017), while eGFR estimates decreased (all p ≤ 0.009). The BUN/creatinine ratio remained unchanged (p ≥ 0.614). However, these within-group findings were descriptive because the corresponding interaction effects were not statistically significant.

Conclusions

In resistance-trained men, 16 weeks of high protein intake did not produce statistically detectable differences in renal biomarker or eGFR changes compared with moderate protein intake, irrespective of training modality. Although modest increases in BUN and cystatin C and small decreases in eGFR estimates were observed within the high-protein groups, these findings were not supported by significant factorial interactions. The limited sample size precludes excluding clinically meaningful differences, warranting further investigation in larger studies.

records.title: Independent and joint associations of physical activity, sedentary behavior, and sleep with vitamin D status in US adults: a cross-sectional NHANES study.
records.publisher: Journal of the International Society of Sports Nutrition

content.title: Independent and joint associations of physical activity, sedentary behavior, and sleep with vitamin D status in US adults: a cross-sectional NHANES study.
content.abstract:
Background

Emerging evidence links movement behaviors to vitamin D status. This study investigated associations between physical activity (PA), sedentary behavior (SB), and sleep with vitamin D status and explored sex differences in these relationships.

Methods

This cross-sectional study included 3195 adults (49.1 ± 17.1 years, 45.5% males) from the 2021-2023 National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey with complete data. Self-reported PA, SB, and sleep duration were assessed. Serum 25-hydroxyvitamin D was measured using high-performance liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry. Generalized linear and logistic regression models were performed.

Results

SB was negatively associated with vitamin D levels in the whole sample (β = -0.006; 95% confidence interval [CI]: -0.012, -0.001) and males (β = -0.008; 95% CI: -0.014, -0.002), but not females. Sleep duration was positively associated with vitamin D among males only (β = 0.023; 95% CI: 0.003, 0.043). Meeting both PA and SB guidelines showed the strongest and most consistent association with vitamin D sufficiency, observed across the whole sample (odds ratio [OR] = 2.129; 95% CI: 1.504, 3.012), males (OR = 2.013; 95% CI: 1.021, 3.967), and females (OR = 2.214; 95% CI: 1.360, 3.605).

Conclusions

Movement behaviors demonstrate independent and joint associations with vitamin D status in US adults, with modest sex-specific patterns that warrant replication. Combined adherence to PA and SB guidelines was consistently associated with greater odds of vitamin D sufficiency across sexes.

records.title: Lower-limb performance and muscle soreness after short-term dark chocolate intake in CrossFit®-trained women: an exploratory secondary analysis.
records.publisher: Journal of the International Society of Sports Nutrition

content.title: Lower-limb performance and muscle soreness after short-term dark chocolate intake in CrossFit®-trained women: an exploratory secondary analysis.
content.abstract:
Background

Dark chocolate (DC) has been proposed as a nutritional aid for exercise performance and recovery, but evidence in trained women remains limited. This exploratory secondary analysis examined selected lower-limb performance outcomes and delayed-onset muscle soreness (DOMS) in female CrossFit® athletes.

Methods

This secondary analysis included 15 trained female CrossFit® athletes from a randomized crossover trial. No separate a priori sample-size calculation was performed for these outcomes (minimum detectable paired effect, d_z = 0.78). DC (30 g/day, 85% cocoa), placebo chocolate (PLA), and an open-label control (CONN) were compared at four operationally defined menstrual-cycle assessments after three days of supplementation. DC-PLA allocation was blinded, but blinding success was not assessed. Outcomes were vertical jump height (VJH), knee isokinetic and isometric performance, and muscle-specific DOMS after the Cindy WOD.

Results

Condition effects survived FDR control for VJH and 19 of 22 dynamometry outcomes. Across assessments, VJH was 34.48 ± 5.09 cm with DC and 30.22 ± 2.34 cm with PLA (mean difference 4.27 cm, 95% CI 1.45 to 7.08; Holm-adjusted p = 0.017; g_av = 1.09). No condition-by-assessment interaction survived FDR control (all q ≥ 0.141). DOMS showed significant time effects for all three muscles, peaked at approximately 24 h, remained elevated at 48 h, and declined toward baseline by 72 h. A condition-by-time effect remained significant only for gastrocnemius soreness (Holm-adjusted p = 0.012; ηp2 = 0.212); no DOMS condition main effect or condition-by-assessment-by-time interaction was supported.

Conclusion

DC was associated with higher values for selected lower-limb outcomes, but these exploratory findings do not establish phase-specific efficacy, equivalent effects across cycle assessments, or a consistent DOMS benefit. Unusually large performance estimates and unmodeled period and carryover effects warrant caution.

records.title: Effects of milk fat globule membrane supplementation on physical function and body composition in older adults: a narrative review.
records.publisher: Journal of the International Society of Sports Nutrition

content.title: Effects of milk fat globule membrane supplementation on physical function and body composition in older adults: a narrative review.
content.abstract:
Background

Healthy aging is a priority for many individuals; however, a decline in physical function and poor body composition are common age-related changes that can cause the added years from rising life expectancy to be spent in poor health. Consequently, understanding the mechanisms involved in aging has become increasingly important, including the role of phospholipids (PLs) and how age-related changes in PL content may interfere with lipid metabolism and normal functioning of the musculoskeletal system. Milk fat globule membrane (MFGM) is a bovine milk fraction rich in PLs that may have the potential to support good physical health, so that quality of life can rise alongside life expectancy.

Methods

This narrative review was based on a literature search conducted on Google Scholar, PubMed, and Scopus in May 2026 using the following keywords and Boolean operators: milk fat globule membrane OR MFGM AND physical function OR body composition OR older adults. Studies were included if they were randomized clinical trials (RCTs) investigating MFGM's effects on physical function and/or body composition in older adults.

Results

Findings suggest that MFGM supplementation, when consumed in conjunction with exercise, is an effective way to improve physical function in older adults, particularly among Japanese cohorts; however, changes in habitual diet in response to exercise, variable PL concentrations, and other added ingredients used in interventions may have influenced these results. In contrast, its effects on body composition appear more modest, with some studies reporting no benefits, especially when exercise was not part of the study design, or when compliance may have been a factor.

Conclusions

Beyond the combined use of supplementation and exercise, future RCTs should consistently report participant compliance and, where possible, examine MFGM as a standalone intervention to distinguish its effects from other bioactive ingredients. Greater standardization is also needed, particularly regarding PL dose. Studies should also aim to include participants from more diverse ethnic backgrounds to capture a wider range of physiological responses and improve generalizability of the findings.

records.title: Effects of extremely low-volume high-intensity interval training combined with iron supplementation versus iron supplementation alone on postural control in young women with iron deficiency anemia: a randomized controlled trial.
records.publisher: Journal of the International Society of Sports Nutrition

content.title: Effects of extremely low-volume high-intensity interval training combined with iron supplementation versus iron supplementation alone on postural control in young women with iron deficiency anemia: a randomized controlled trial.
content.abstract:
Background

Recent research revealed postural control deterioration in young women with Iron Deficiency Anemia (IDA). To address this postural deficit, it is crucial to develop intervention strategies for postural rehabilitation in these individuals. This study aimed to explore the effect of 8-week extremely low-volume high-intensity interval training (HIIT) based on plyometric exercises combined with iron supplementation versus simple iron treatment on postural control of young women with IDA.

Methods

This randomized controlled trial enrolled young women with IDA aged 18-25 years, who were randomly assigned to a training group (TG; n = 16) or a non-training group (NTG; n = 17). All participants received oral iron supplementation (ferrous sulfate, 494.5 mg/day, administered as 247.25 mg twice daily), while the TG additionally completed an 8-week extremely low-volume HIIT program based on plyometric exercises. Hemoglobin (Hb) and serum ferritin concentrations were assessed, alongside muscle endurance, reaction time performance, and postural control. Muscle endurance was evaluated using the Killy test, reaction time performance using an online simple reaction time test, and postural control using a stabilometric platform under bipodal and semi-tandem stance conditions. Postural assessments were conducted with eyes open (EO) and eyes closed (EC) on firm and foam surfaces. All outcomes were measured at baseline and 72 h after the final intervention session.

Results

After the 8-week intervention, this study demonstrated significant improvements across both groups, irrespective of the intervention. However, TG showed significantly greater post-intervention improvements than NTG in Hb concentration (P = 0.042), muscle endurance (P < 0.001), and postural control. Superior postural control in TG was observed during a bipedal stance on a foam surface (EO: P = 0.001); EC: P = 0.035), as well as during semi-tandem stance on a firm surface (EO: P = 0.015; EC: P = 0.040) and on a foam surface (EO: P = 0.019; EC: P = 0.003), compared to the NTG. With a Bonferroni-adjusted significance threshold for multiple comparisons (α = 0.00625), between-group differences in postural control remained significant for bipedal foam EO (P = 0.001) and semi-tandem foam EC (P = 0.003).

Conclusions

The study showed that women with IDA improved their postural performance regardless of the intervention used. However, an 8-week program of extremely low-volume HIIT combined with plyometric exercises and iron supplementation had a more beneficial effect compared to traditional iron therapy. These greater improvements in postural control occurred alongside greater improvements in the Hb concentration and muscle endurance in the TG compared to the NTG.

records.title: Efficacy of exercise interventions on prevention of sport-related concussion and related outcomes: a systematic review and meta-analysis.

content.title: Efficacy of exercise interventions on prevention of sport-related concussion and related outcomes: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
content.abstract:
Objective

To review the efficacy of exercise interventions on sport-related concussion (SRC) incidence, as well as on linear and rotational head accelerations, and isometric neck strength and to assess reporting completeness of exercise interventions using the Consensus on Exercise Reporting Template (CERT).

Design

Systematic review and meta-analysis, according to the Prisma in Exercise, Rehabilitation, Sport medicine and SporTs science guidelines.

Data sources

Six databases (MEDLINE, Embase, CINAHL, Scopus, Web of Science CC and SPORTDiscus) were searched up to 26 June 2023.

Eligibility criteria for selecting studies

Randomised controlled trials (RCTs), cluster RCTs or quasi-experimental studies, evaluating exercise interventions on SRC incidence, linear and rotational head accelerations, and/or isometric neck strength in male and/or female athletes of any age, and/or in a healthy general population.

Results

A total of 26 articles were included. A large effect size was observed for resistance training (RT) on isometric neck strength (standardised mean difference (SMD) 0.85; 95% CI 0.57 to 1.13; high-quality evidence).
